https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/i.title: In Makkah, Tinubu Puts His Re-election in Allah’s Hands
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/i.summary: At the Holy Ka’abah, Tinubu offered prayers of gratitude to the Almighty Allah for the privilege of serving as Nigeria’s President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces. Tinubu thanked the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, for granting him and members of his delegation the opportunity to enter the Holy Ka’abah in Makkah and offer prayers to Almighty Allah.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/i.summary_zh: 在神圣的麦加大清真寺，蒂努布感谢至大的真安赐予其担任尼日利亚总统兼武装部队总司令的殊荣，并为此祈祷。他感谢两座圣寺的守护者萨勒曼·本·阿卜杜勒阿齐兹·阿沙特国王以及王储穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼，感谢他们给予他及其代表团进入位于麦加的神圣麦加大清真寺、向至大的真安祈祷的机会。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/i.body: •Recommits to building a prosperous nation, says Nigeria will overcome challenges Deji Elumoye, Chuks Okocha in Abuja and Benjamin Nworie in Abakaliki In supplication and total submission to the Almighty, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, yesterday, at the Holy Ka’abah, Mecca, where he had gone to observe Umrah, the lesser hajj, handed his re-election challenges to Allah, in whom he trusted. With a tinge of drama, Tinubu, who held and kissed the Al-Hajar al-Aswad otherwise called the Black Stone, in a symbolic sunnah, often performed in emulation of the Prophet Mohammad, however, prayed for wisdom and strength. The Black Stone is one of the most sacred objects in Islam, embedded in the southeastern corner of the Holy Ka’abah in Makkah, Saudi Arabia, surrounded by a silver frame. Muslims hold it in great reverence because Islamic tradition teaches that it came from paradise and that Prophet Mohammad kissed it. It is therefore an expression of faith and reverence, not an act of worshipping the stone. The president, who concluded his five-day visit to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, reflected on his spiritual journey to the Holy land, during which the Custodian of the Holy Mosques of Makkah and Madinah, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, granted him a rare privilege of leading Nigeria’s delegation to pray inside the Holy Ka’abah. At the Holy Ka’abah, Tinubu offered prayers of gratitude to the Almighty Allah for the privilege of serving as Nigeria’s President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces. Sheikh Dahlulah Muthawal of Masjid al-Haram led the president into the Ka’abah. Tinubu thanked the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, for granting him and members of his delegation the opportunity to enter the Holy Ka’abah in Makkah and offer prayers to Almighty Allah. The president described the honour as a historic and deeply cherished spiritual experience, reflecting the longstanding bonds of friendship, mutual respect and cooperation between Nigeria and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. “I want to say a big thank you for the faith, for the recognition. I can’t believe the fencing of the Ka’abah is in Green-White-Green, which reminds us of the Nigerian identity. “I thank the Crown Prince and all the administrators of the holy land. I thank them for the hospitality and recognition given to me as the leader of the delegation and the country. “We are all facing challenges and hostility around us. We will overcome them with faith in God Almighty. I’m grateful forever. I thank the King and the royal Crown Prince. “It is an honour that I enjoyed, and it is gracious of them to have allowed me to enter inside the Ka’abah. This is history.” Tinubu said he asked Allah for wisdom and resilience to continue serving Nigerians, and expressed confidence that his prayers have been answered. According to him, “I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that prayer has been granted. Before the 2023 election, I did the same thing. I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then, and He did. And I promised that I would come back to thank Him.” He reflected on the message from the Holy Qur’an in Surah Aal-Imran, Verse 26, which affirmed that Almighty Allah is the Owner of all sovereignty, granting power and authority to whom He wills and taking them away from whom He wills. The president said power is a trust that must be exercised responsibly, with humility and in the service of the people, recognising that no position of authority is permanent and that ultimate sovereignty belongs to Almighty Allah. “There is no other God but Almighty Allah. He is the giver and the taker. He owns power and authority. He says, ‘If I give you, use it well. If you don’t use it in accordance with my dictates, I can take it from you and give it to another person. I am the only One who has that authority,” the president said, quoting the Qur’an. Tinubu said faith in Allah had strengthened his conviction that his emergence as Nigeria’s leader was an extraordinary blessing that must be matched with dedicated service to the country. “I have faith in that, and I believe extremely well that He has done me and my country a great favour. Out of many millions of people, to be the President and Commander-in-Chief is a favour that only Almighty God can do to a human being,” he stated. Tinubu reiterated his commitment to Project Nigeria and his determination to build a prosperous nation, invest in the future of young Nigerians, and pursue development in line with the will of Almighty Allah and the people’s aspirations. He emphasised that his commitment to Project Nigeria had become even stronger, assuring Nigerians of his resolve to pursue policies and programmes that would promote prosperity, national development and shared progress. “My commitment to Project Nigeria is higher. I am determined to usher in prosperity and fully develop the country, consistent with the wish of Allah and the support of the people. “It is important to put Allah first, then move on. Follow your conscience. Follow the right path that will lead Nigeria to that greatness,” Tinubu said. On the nation’s economic outlook, the president expressed optimism about the progress made under his watch, describing the economic foundation as solid and the country’s emergence from a difficult period as encouraging. “The foundation is solid, and the economy has come out of the dark tunnel. This is inspiring.” He maintained, however, that nation-building required sustained investment in young Nigerians’ future, noting that today’s leaders’ decisions would determine how future generations remember them. “We need to build a future for our youth. If we don’t invest in their future, how do we want to be remembered as leaders 50 years from now? That’s the main thing. So this is a rare privilege to lead the country,” he added. Tinubu reiterated that his administration would remain focused on strengthening the country’s economic foundations, expanding opportunities for young people and creating the conditions necessary for Nigerians to realise their potential. The president thanked Almighty Allah for the opportunity to lead Nigeria and reaffirmed his determination to justify the confidence the Nigerian people have placed in him through purposeful leadership and an enduring commitment to national progress. Earlier, the President, had disclosed on X @OfficialPBAT, that he had concluded his visit to Saudi, adding that he used the opportunity of the visit to pray for peace, unity and prosperity to reign supreme in Nigeria. Tinubu, according to the four-paragraph post, stated: “I have concluded my visit to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, where, together with members of my delegation, I had the rare honour of entering the Holy Kaaba to pray, and of performing Umrah. “I am deeply grateful to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud @KingSalman, and to Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman for extending this privilege to us, and for their gracious hospitality and brotherly care. “It reflects the enduring bonds of faith and friendship between Nigeria and Saudi Arabia. In those sacred moments, I prayed for peace, unity and prosperity for our dear nation and for all Nigerians.” The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organization (MDPCO) has berated President Bola Tinubu for allegedly falsely claiming in Mecca that Nigeria’s economy has “come out of the dark tunnel” when in reality the economy was worsening by the day. The Makinde/Daura presidential campaigns said it was profane that President Tinubu could stand before the Holy Ka’abah in Makkah to make such a spurious claim despite the damming indices showing that the nation was sinking deeper into poverty under him with over 140 million citizens (63% of the population) living in abject poverty. In a statement, the Director of Strategic Communication of the Makinde/Daura presidential campaign, Richard Ihediuwa, said, ‘’While President Tinubu made his false claims in Mecca, hundreds of businesses are closing on daily basis in Nigeria due to the adverse effect of his punishing economic policies and harsh taxes. ‘’Despite being an oil producing country, fuel price in Nigeria remains unaffordable at N1,500 to N2,000 per liter in various parts of the country, driving high costs of living, harsh business environment and eroded purchasing power of citizens. ‘’Today, under President Tinubu’s voodoo economy Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit has hit an estimated $2.3 trillion, with experts stating that the gap would require approximately $100 billion annually over the next 30 years to fix. ‘’The fact that President Tinubu can, in the face of the current economic quagmire, claim that the nation economy has come out of the dark tunnel, only goes to confirm that he has come to his wits end and has nothing more to offer as president. ‘’His affirmation in the Holy Land that the Almighty Allah gives power and can take from him to whom He wills, comes to Nigerians as an answered prayer given their earnest desire and supplication for a breath of fresh air under a new leadership,’’ the statement said. The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), South East zone as well as the Hausa and Yoruba communities in Ebonyi State, have endorsed President Tinubu for re-election in the 2027 elections. The different bodies made the endorsement yesterday in Abakaliki during a Town Hall meeting powered by the Directorate of Infrastructure, Mobilisation and Sensitisation of All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council (PCC). Addressing members of the association, the President of the Christian Fellowship of Nigeria (CFN), South East zone, Rev. Fr. Abraham Nwali, appreciated the president for uplifting the zone through massive infrastructure. He urged the members of the association and the entire people of the zone to support Tinubu’s re-election as mark of appreciation for his love for the region. “We are owing our leader the president and Minister of Works, His Excellency, Senator David Umahi, appreciation, and the only way we can show the appreciation is to support the president in the 2027 general election,” Nwali stated. A former President of the Women Wing of the association, Mrs. Uche Charity Ujunwa, said Tinubu has brought reforms to the country which was impacting positively on the people and called for support of the President in the 2027 general election. Leader of the Youth Wing of CAN South East, Peter Onyeabor, assured the president that the entire Christian youths in the zone would deliver the president in the general election. On their parts, Kazeem Bankole, leader of Yoruba community in Ebonyi and Alhaji Danjuma Gambo, leader of Hausa community in the state, declared that they would mobilise the communities to deliver Tinubu and all the APC candidates in the general election. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/i.title_zh: 在麦加，提努布将连任希望交由真主裁决
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/i.body_zh:
•承诺建设繁荣国家；尼日利亚将克服挑战——德吉·埃卢莫耶、阿布贾的楚克斯·奥科查以及阿巴卡利基的本杰明·恩沃里耶

在向全能至高的真主祈祷、彻底皈依之际，总统博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布昨天在麦加的禁寺——他此行前往是为了瞻礼 lesser hajj（小朝觐）——将自己连任选举中的挑战托付给他所信赖的安拉。带着几分戏剧性，蒂努布依照先知穆罕默德经常举行的象征性圣行，手持并亲吻了Al-Hajar al-Aswad（又称黑石），但他祈祷的是智慧与力量。黑石是伊斯兰教最神圣的圣物之一，嵌在沙特阿拉伯麦加禁寺东南角，周围环绕着银制框架。穆斯林对黑石极为尊崇，因为伊斯兰传统教导人们，黑石来自天堂，先知穆罕默德曾亲吻过它。因此，这一举动表达的是信仰和敬意，而不是对石头的崇拜。

这位结束了对沙特阿拉伯王国为期5天访问的总统，回顾了自己前往圣地的精神历程。在这段行程中，麦加和麦地那两座圣寺的守护者——萨勒曼·本·阿卜杜勒阿齐兹·阿尔·沙特国王——赋予他一项殊荣，让他率领尼日利亚代表团进入禁寺祈祷。在禁寺内，蒂努布感谢全能至高的安拉，感谢祂让自己有幸担任尼日利亚总统和武装部队总司令。禁寺伊玛目Sheikh Dahlulah Muthawal引导总统进入禁寺。蒂努布感谢两座圣寺的守护者萨勒曼·本·阿卜杜勒阿齐兹·阿尔·沙特国王，以及王储兼首相穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼，感谢他们让他和代表团成员获准进入麦加禁寺，向全能至高的安拉祈祷。总统称，这份荣誉是一次具有历史意义、深受珍视的精神体验，体现了尼日利亚与沙特阿拉伯王国之间长期牢固的友谊、相互尊重与合作。

“我要向这份信任和这份认可表示衷心感谢。我简直不敢相信禁寺的围栏采用了绿—白—绿三色，这让我们想起尼日利亚的身份认同。

“我感谢王储和圣地的所有管理人员。我感谢他们给予我这个代表团领袖和国家领导人的款待与认可。

“我们都面临着种种挑战和敌意。我们将凭借对全能上帝的信仰克服这些挑战。我永远心怀感激。我感谢国王和王储。

“我有幸享受这份礼遇，他们恩准我进入禁寺，这是历史性的时刻。”

蒂努布表示，他向安拉祈求智慧和韧性，以继续服务尼日利亚人民，并相信自己的祈祷已获应答。据他说：“我祈求智慧和韧性，以继续为人民服务。我知道祈祷已经得到应允。2023年大选前我也这样做过。我当时请求安拉赐福我的小朝觐，祂应允了。我还承诺会回来向祂致谢。”

他回顾了《古兰经》第三篇《伊姆兰家族章》第26节中的教义，指出全能至高的安拉是一切主权的主宰，将权力和权威赐予祂所意欲的人，也从祂所意欲的人手中收回权力。总统表示，权力是一种信任，必须以谦逊和负责的态度运用于为人民服务，同时认识到任何权威职位都不是永久的，最终主权属于全能至高的安拉。

“除全能至高的安拉外，别无神明。祂是赐予者，也是收回者。祂拥有权力和权威。祂说：‘如果我赐予你，就要善用它。如果你不依照我的旨意使用它，我可以从你手中收回，赐予另一个人。只有我拥有这种权威。’”总统在引用《古兰经》时说。

蒂努布表示，对安拉的信仰强化了他的信念：他成为尼日利亚领导人是莫大的恩赐，必须以对国家的无私奉献来回应。他说：“我对此充满信心，也坚信祂已赐予我和我的国家莫大的恩惠。在数以百万计的人中，成为总统和武装部队总司令，是全能上帝才会赐予一个世人的恩惠。”

蒂努布再次承诺推进“尼日利亚计划”，并决心建设繁荣国家、投资于尼日利亚青年的未来，按照全能至高的安拉的旨意和人民的愿望推进发展。他强调，他对“尼日利亚计划”的承诺变得更加坚定，并向尼日利亚人民保证，他决心推行促进繁荣、国家发展和共同进步的政策与方案。

“我对‘尼日利亚计划’的承诺更加坚定。我决心开创繁荣局面，全面发展国家，以符合安拉的意愿和人民的支持。

“最重要的是把安拉放在首位，然后继续前进。遵循你们的良知，走上通往尼日利亚伟大未来的正确道路。”蒂努布说。

谈及国家经济前景，总统对其任内取得的进展表示乐观，称经济基础坚实，国家走出困难时期令人鼓舞。“基础坚实，经济已经走出黑暗隧道。这令人振奋。”不过他坚持认为，国家建设需要持续投资尼日利亚青年的未来，并指出，今天领导人的决定将决定后世如何铭记他们。

“我们需要为青年建设未来。如果不投资他们的未来，我们希望50年后作为领导人被人们如何铭记？这一点最为重要。因此，领导这个国家是一份难得的殊荣。”他补充说。

蒂努布再次强调，其政府将继续专注于加强国家经济基础，为年轻人拓展机会，并创造必要条件，让尼日利亚人民实现自身潜能。总统感谢全能至高的安拉给予他领导尼日利亚的机会，并重申决心通过有目标的领导和对国家进步的持久承诺，回报尼日利亚人民对他的信任。

早先，总统在X平台账号@OfficialPBAT上披露，他已结束对沙特的访问，并表示利用此次访问机会为和平、统一和繁荣祈祷，希望这些美好事物在尼日利亚占据主导地位。根据蒂努布发布的四段帖文，他表示：“我已结束对沙特阿拉伯王国的访问。在那里，我与代表团成员有幸进入天房祈祷并完成小朝觐。

“我衷心感谢两座圣寺的守护者萨勒曼·本·阿卜杜勒阿齐兹·阿尔·沙特国王@KingSalman，以及王储兼首相穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼，感谢他们给予我们这一殊荣，以及他们盛情的款待和兄弟般的关怀。

“这体现了尼日利亚与沙特阿拉伯之间持久的信仰与友谊纽带。在那些神圣时刻，我为我们亲爱的国家和全体尼日利亚人民祈求和平、统一与繁荣。”

马金德—达乌拉总统竞选组织（MDPCO）批评博拉·蒂努布总统，称他据称在麦加虚假宣称尼日利亚经济已经“走出黑暗隧道”，而实际上经济正日益恶化。马金德／达乌拉总统竞选团队称，蒂努布总统竟能站在麦加禁寺前作出如此虚假言论，而一系列严峻数据表明，在他的治下，全国有超过1.4亿国民（占总人口的63%）生活在赤贫之中，这亵渎了圣地。

在一份声明中，马金德／达乌拉总统竞选组织战略传播主任理查德·伊赫迪乌瓦表示：“蒂努布总统在麦加作出虚假宣称的同时，尼日利亚每天都有数百家企业因他严苛的经济政策和重税造成的不利影响而关门。

“尽管尼日利亚是石油生产国，但全国多地的燃油价格仍高不可攀，每升达到N1,500至N2,000，推高了生活成本，造成恶劣的商业环境，并削弱公民购买力。

“如今，在蒂努布总统所谓‘巫毒经济’之下，尼日利亚的基础设施缺口估计已达2.3万亿美元。专家表示，弥补这一缺口在未来30年内每年约需投入1,000亿美元。

“面对当前经济困境，蒂努布总统竟声称国家经济已经走出黑暗隧道，这只会证明他已经无计可施，作为总统再也拿不出任何东西。

“他在圣地确认全能至高的安拉赐予权力，也能从祂意欲的人手中收回权力。对尼日利亚人民而言，这一说法听起来就像是祈祷得到了应允，因为大家真诚期盼在新领导层治下迎来一口新鲜空气。”声明说。

尼日利亚基督教协会（CAN）东南区，以及埃博尼州的豪萨族和约鲁巴族社群，均表示支持蒂努布总统参加2027年连任竞选。这些不同机构昨天在阿巴卡利基举行的一场市民大会会议上作出支持决定。此次大会由全进步大会党（APC）总统竞选委员会（PCC）基础设施、动员与宣传局推动召开。

在向协会成员发表讲话时，尼日利亚基督教团契（CFN）东南区主席Abraham Nwali神父对总统通过大规模基础设施建设提升该地区状况表示赞赏。他敦促协会成员和该地区全体人民支持蒂努布连任，以表达对该地区所获关爱的感谢。

“我们欠我们的领袖——总统兼工程部长、尊敬的David Umahi参议员——一份感谢，而表达感谢的唯一方式，就是在2027年大选中支持总统。”Nwali说。

该协会妇女翼前主席Uche Charity Ujunwa女士表示，蒂努布为这个国家带来了改革，这些改革正对人民产生积极影响，并呼吁支持总统参加2027年大选。CAN东南区青年翼领袖Peter Onyeabor向总统保证，该地区全体基督教青年将在大选中支持总统。埃博尼州约鲁巴族社群领袖Kazeem Bankole和该州豪萨族社群领袖Alhaji Danjuma Gambo分别表示，他们将动员各自社群，在大选中支持蒂努布及所有APC候选人。

But Osifo countered that discussions on workers’ welfare and the allowance had begun long before Ajaero’s meeting with government, adding that government had separately engaged the TUC. But in a reply after Ajaero’s interview, Osifo fired back strongly, saying the labour movement deserved better leadership and that Ajaero deserved to be pitied.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/n.summary_zh: 这为两大劳工中心之间的冲突定了调子。不过，Osifo反驳称，关于工人福利和津贴的讨论早在Ajaero与政府会面之前就已开始，政府还另行与TUC进行了接触。Ajaero接受采访后，Osifo在回应中强烈反击，称劳工运动本应得到更好的领导，Ajaero则值得同情。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/n.body: The disagreement, which centred on the six-month palliative announced by the Bola Tinubu administration, played out on Channels Television’s breakfast programme, where both labour leaders took turns to attack each other’s credibility and negotiating capacity. Last Tuesday, the federal government had announced the transport allowance in a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) issued after a meeting between government representatives and NLC leaders in Abuja. Barely 24 hours after the announcement, the TUC rejected the allowance, insisting that what Nigerian workers needed was a salary increase, not a temporary palliative. This set the tone for a clash between the two labour centres. Reacting to the TUC’s position, Ajaero said the trade union led by Osifo ought to have negotiated its own terms with government rather than disown the outcome of a negotiation it did not participate in. But Osifo countered that discussions on workers’ welfare and the allowance had begun long before Ajaero’s meeting with government, adding that government had separately engaged the TUC. However, speaking on the programme yesterday, Ajaero maintained that the N70,000 allowance was the product of collective bargaining triggered by an ultimatum issued by the NLC. “When he (Osifo) said I did not negotiate N70,000 transport allowance, I did not know what he meant. We (NLC) gave the government an ultimatum and the government asked for four days to meet with us. “At the resumed sitting after four days, some agreements were reached. After every collective bargaining, the product is the agreement. It was in that agreement that the issue of N70,000 was reached,” he said. Ajaero went further to question Osifo’s stewardship of the TUC and the whereabouts of the 90 Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) buses donated to the TUC by the federal government. Describing Osifo as an “absentee president,” Ajaero alleged that the TUC leader does not reside in Nigeria and was only running the union from abroad. “He is an absentee president of the TUC. He does not live in Nigeria. He comes in from the US to attend meetings and rush back. He serves in the board of PENCOM. You cannot be living abroad and be holding a position in a central level organisation. I challenge him and the Nigeria Immigration Service to prove if he has been in this country for four to five months this year,” he added. But in a reply after Ajaero’s interview, Osifo fired back strongly, saying the labour movement deserved better leadership and that Ajaero deserved to be pitied. He described the NLC chief as a disaster. Besides, Osifo said the labour movement deserved some pity too after listening to the NLC president, noting that the movement once boasted great leaders. “I can boldly say that Joe Ajaero is a disaster to the trade union movement in Nigeria,” Osifo said. The TUC president insisted that the NLC could not negotiate on behalf of TUC members, as the congress remains a recognised federation with its own affiliates and mandate. On the allegation that he lives outside the country, Osifo said it was a shame that such a claim would come from the NLC president. He disclosed that before handing over as President of the Petroleum and Natural Gas Senior Staff Association of Nigeria (PENGASSAN) in August, he shuttled from one shop floor to another negotiating salary increments for members. Osifo said he was currently in the United Kingdom for training on advanced leadership and management and accused Ajaero of shortchanging Nigerian workers on account of poor negotiation skills. “Ajaero has never led any union in Nigeria that is why he does not understand the principles of negotiation,” Osifo said. “What I will recommend for him is training and retraining,” he added. For years, although the labour unions have had their differences, they have struggled to speak with one voice on major issues that affect workers. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/n.body_zh: 这场分歧的焦点，是博拉·蒂努布政府宣布发放的六个月临时补助；分歧在Channels Television的早餐节目中展开，两名劳工领袖轮流攻击对方的可信度和谈判能力。上周二，联邦政府在一份谅解备忘录中宣布了交通补贴，该备忘录是在政府代表与阿布贾全国劳工大会（NLC）领导人会面后发布的。公告发布不到24小时，工会大会（TUC）便拒绝了这项补贴，坚持认为尼日利亚工人需要的是加薪，而不是临时救济。这为两大劳工中心之间的冲突定下了基调。针对TUC的立场，阿杰罗表示，由奥西福领导的工会本应自行与政府谈判条件，而不是否认自己未参与的谈判结果。奥西福则反驳称，关于工人福利和补贴的讨论早在阿杰罗与政府会面之前就已开始，政府还单独与TUC进行了磋商。然而，阿杰罗昨天在节目中仍坚持认为，N70,000补贴是NLC发出最后通牒后启动集体谈判的成果。他说：“当他说我并未谈下N70,000交通补贴时，我不知道他是什么意思。我们（NLC）向政府发出了最后通牒，政府要求给我们4天时间会面。“4天后复会时，我们达成了一些协议。每次集体谈判结束后，成果就是达成的协议。N70,000的问题正是在该协议中确定的。”阿杰罗进一步质疑奥西福对TUC的领导，并追问联邦政府捐赠给TUC的90辆压缩天然气（CNG）巴士究竟去向何处。阿杰罗称奥西福为“缺席的主席”，指控这位TUC领导人并不居住在尼日利亚，只在国外远程管理工会。他说：“他是TUC的缺席主席。他不住在尼日利亚。他从美国来这里参加会议，然后匆匆返回。他在PENCOM担任董事会成员。你不可能既住在国外，又在一家全国性组织中任职。我要他和尼日利亚移民局证明，他今年是否曾在这个国家待过4至5个月。”不过，在阿杰罗采访结束后回应时，奥西福强硬反击，称劳工运动本应得到更好的领导，而阿杰罗则值得同情。他形容NLC主席是一场灾难。奥西福说，听完NLC主席的表态后，劳工运动也值得同情，因为该运动曾经拥有杰出的领袖。奥西福说：“我可以大胆地说，乔·阿杰罗是尼日利亚工会运动的一场灾难。”TUC主席坚持认为，NLC不能代表TUC成员进行谈判，因为TUC大会仍是一个得到承认的联合会，拥有自己的附属组织和授权。对于自己居住在国外的说法，奥西福表示，这种指控竟由NLC主席提出，实在令人遗憾。他透露，在8月将尼日利亚石油和天然气高级职员协会（PENGASSAN）主席职务移交给别人之前，他曾往返于各个基层工作场所，为协会成员争取加薪。奥西福称，他目前正在英国接受高级领导力和管理方面的培训，并指责阿杰罗因谈判能力拙劣而亏待尼日利亚工人。奥西福说：“阿杰罗从未领导过尼日利亚的任何工会，因此他不理解谈判原则。”“我给他的建议是接受培训并重新培训。”多年来，尽管各工会之间存在分歧，但在影响工人的重大议题上，它们一直难以发出统一声音。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创刊，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕溪路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区以及世界各地设有办事处。作为尼日利亚最权威的新闻媒体，该报通过全平台为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级服务，同时充当有抱负者和千禧一代连接新思想、文化与技术的交汇点。这份报纸是一项公共信任，致力于追求真相与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育、社区，以及人与社会的交汇点。您可以发送电子邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/o.summary: The 2027 governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ogun State, Senator Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, has pledged to develop a vibrant creative economy and create an enabling environment for young talents to thrive and secure employment within the state if elected governor. Adeola made the pledge in Abeokuta during an interactive session with a cross-section of Ogun youths.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/o.summary_zh: 全进步大会党（APC）奥贡州2027年州长候选人Solomon Adeola参议员（广为人知的Yayi）承诺，如果当选州长，将发展充满活力的创意经济，并为年轻人才在该州成长和就业营造有利环境。Adeola是在阿贝奥库塔与奥贡州部分青年举行互动活动时作出这一承诺的。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/o.body: The 2027 governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ogun State, Senator Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, has pledged to develop a vibrant creative economy and create an enabling environment for young talents to thrive and secure employment within the state if elected governor. Adeola made the pledge in Abeokuta during an interactive session with a cross-section of Ogun youths. Speaking at the session themed “Gen Z Asks, Yayi Listens,” Adeola noted that Ogun State is home to immense talent and promised to establish platforms that would help young people discover, develop and showcase their abilities. In her opening remarks, the convener of Gen Z for Yayi, Kira Taiwo, described the session as an opportunity for young people to contribute to conversations about their future and the development of Ogun State. She said the engagement was designed to give youths a platform to express the opportunities they would like to see under the next administration. “I hope this translates to youth participation and opportunities to shape the future of Ogun State,” Taiwo said. Responding Adeola said his administration would strengthen the Ministry of Culture and Tourism to drive talent discovery, promotion and the growth of the state’s creative economy. He said, “Under the nine pillars of my administration, we are giving focus to cultural and tourism. We will empower the ministry of Culture and Tourism to create a platform that will detect and promote talents. “We will ensure a ministry that is efficient and vibrant. We will work closely with talents and stakeholders to create a thriving creative and entertainment industry in Ogun State.” On youth unemployment and underemployment, the senator pledged to negotiate employment quotas with industries operating in the state to create opportunities for qualified indigenes. He added that available positions would be publicly advertised and made accessible to eligible graduates. Addressing concerns about the growing trend of young Nigerians seeking opportunities abroad, popularly known as ‘Japa’, Adeola acknowledged that it had become a national challenge. He said his administration would tackle the trend in Ogun State by creating well-paying jobs and improving opportunities for young professionals. “Especially in the medical profession, Ogun State needs more doctors and qualified nurses. We will work closely with them to make sure they are employed within this system. The APC candidate assured the youths that the initiatives on infrastructural projects would continue and expand if elected. “I have set a standard that I can’t go below. I will improve on my development programmes. We will set up the Ministry of Wealth Creation that will drive the Continuity of my empowerment programmes. “We will empower more people across the state and also embark on skill acquisition programmes that will upscale capacity. Under my leadership, the issue of bad roads will be a thing of the past in Ogun State. No student will study under the tree during my tenure as governor of this state,” Senator Adeola said. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/o.title_zh: 奥贡州2027年选举：阿德奥拉承诺打造充满活力的创意经济，为奥贡州青年创造就业机会
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/o.body_zh: 奥贡州全体进步大会党（APC）2027年州长候选人、参议员Solomon Adeola（广为人知的Yayi）承诺，如果当选州长，将大力发展充满活力的创意经济，并营造有利环境，让年轻人才在州内成长并获得就业。Adeola在Abeokuta与奥贡州青年代表举行互动活动时作出上述承诺。他在题为“Gen Z Asks, Yayi Listens”的活动上表示，奥贡州拥有众多杰出人才，并承诺建立平台，帮助年轻人发现、培养和展示自身能力。Gen Z for Yayi活动召集人Kira Taiwo在开幕致辞中表示，此次活动为年轻人提供了参与讨论自身未来及奥贡州发展的机会。她说，这项交流旨在为青年提供一个平台，让他们表达希望下一届政府任内能够提供的机会。Taiwo说：“我希望这能转化为青年广泛参与，并获得塑造奥贡州未来的机会。”Adeola回应称，他的政府将强化文化与旅游部，以推动人才发现、推广以及该州创意经济增长。他说：“在我的政府九大支柱中，我们重点关注文化和旅游。我们将赋能文化与旅游部，打造发现和推广人才的平台。我们将确保该部高效运转、充满活力。我们将与人才和相关利益方密切合作，在奥贡州打造繁荣的创意与娱乐产业。”谈及青年失业和就业不足问题，这位参议员承诺与州内各行业协商就业配额，为符合资格的本地人创造就业机会。他补充说，现有职位将公开招聘，并向符合条件的毕业生开放。针对越来越多的尼日利亚年轻人赴海外寻找机会这一日益盛行的趋势，即通常所说的“Japa”，Adeola承认这已成为全国性挑战。他说，他的政府将通过创造高薪岗位和改善年轻专业人士的就业机会，应对奥贡州的这一趋势。他表示：“尤其是在医疗卫生领域，奥贡州需要更多医生和具备资格的护士。我们将与他们密切合作，确保他们能在本州医疗体系内就业。”这位APC候选人向青年保证，如果当选，基础设施项目的相关举措将得以延续并扩大。Adeola参议员说：“我已经设定了不能降低的标准。我会改进我的发展计划。我们将设立财富创造部，推动我各项赋能计划的延续。我们将在全州赋能更多人，同时开展技能提升计划，增强人员能力。在我的领导下，道路破败问题将在奥贡州成为过去。我担任该州州长期间，不会再有学生在树下上课。”THISDAY创刊于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，社址位于尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕Creek Road 35号，并在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都领地及世界各地设有办事处。该报是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，通过全平台服务政界、商界、专业人士和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶层，同时为有志者和千禧一代提供新思想、文化与技术的交汇平台。这份报纸秉持公共信托精神，致力于追求真相与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育、社区，以及人与社会的交汇点。您可以发送邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/j.summary_zh: Johnvents Industries Limited已在到期时全额赎回其第21期商业票据，票据面值总额为286.4亿奈拉；同时，其800亿奈拉第1期商业票据发行获得超额认购。公司在周一发布的声明中披露了上述情况，并说明赎回已按照相关工具的条款完成。此次新发行在其2500亿奈拉商业票据计划下推出 attracts 的认购额高于发行规模。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/j.body: Johnvents Industries Limited has fully redeemed its Series 21 Commercial Paper, with an aggregate face value of N28.64 billion, at maturity, while recording an oversubscription of its N80 billion Series 1 Commercial Paper issuance. The company disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday, explaining the redemption was completed in accordance with the terms of the instrument, while the fresh issuance, floated under its N250 billion Commercial Paper Programme, attracted subscriptions above the offer size. The twin developments, according to the company, demonstrate its commitment to meeting financial obligations, maintaining liquidity discipline and sustaining access to the domestic capital market to finance its expanding operations. The successful issuance comes as Johnvents intensifies efforts to expand its operations, increase processing capacity and strengthen its position across Nigeria’s agricultural value chain. The proceeds from the N80 billion issuance will be deployed to support seasonal working capital requirements, particularly the procurement and processing of cocoa and other agricultural commodities during the current operating cycle. The company explained that the funding would enable it to secure raw materials within critical seasonal windows and sustain operations across its processing facilities, ensuring continuity in its commodity sourcing, processing and shipment activities. Speaking on the development, the Group Managing Director, John Alamu, described the oversubscription as a strong vote of confidence in the company’s vision of connecting agriculture with industry, exports and consumer markets. He said, “The response to this issuance is an important vote of confidence in what Johnvents is building: a Nigerian business that connects agriculture to industry, exports and everyday consumer products. “Our ambition is to create more value locally and build a company capable of competing across markets. That confidence also places a responsibility on us to execute with discipline.” Alamu assured investors that the proceeds would be applied in accordance with the approved offer documents, while the company would sustain its focus on liquidity management and timely fulfilment of repayment obligations. The Group Head of Treasury, Samuel Olaifa, said the successful issuance, alongside the full redemption of Series 21 at maturity, reflected the company’s deliberate approach to managing its funding requirements and repayment obligations. He explained that the transactions were structured around the company’s seasonal working capital cycle, particularly the procurement, processing and shipment of cocoa and other agricultural commodities. The company disclosed that the transaction followed an extensive investor engagement programme, including management meetings and tours of selected Johnvents facilities, which enabled investors to assess its operations, processing capacity, inventory cycle and integrated value chain. The Acting Managing Director of Regius Capital, Kayode Omosebi, said the engagements provided investors with a clearer understanding of the relationship between the company’s operating assets, inventory cycle, cash generation and repayment capacity. He noted the oversubscription reflected institutional appetite for well-structured credit opportunities, as well as the importance of transparent engagement between companies and investors. The company said its next phase of growth would focus on increasing processing throughput, improving capacity utilisation, expanding into higher-value consumer goods and strengthening domestic distribution and export relationships. He added that its expansion strategy was also designed to strengthen Nigeria’s non-oil export base, create employment opportunities and support businesses across its network of farmers, aggregators, transporters, distributors and service providers. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/j.title_zh: Johnvents偿还286.4亿奈拉债务，800亿奈拉商业票据获超额认购
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/j.body_zh: Johnvents Industries Limited已在到期时全额赎回其第21期商业票据，面值总额为N28.64 billion；与此同时，其N80 billion第1期商业票据发行获得超额认购。该公司在周一发布的声明中披露了上述情况，说明赎回已按照相关工具的条款完成，而此次新发行属于其N250 billion商业票据计划的一部分，认购额超过发行规模。据公司介绍，这两项进展体现了公司履行财务义务、保持流动性纪律以及持续进入国内资本市场，为不断扩大的业务运营提供融资的承诺。此次成功发行之际，Johnvents正加大力度拓展业务、提高加工产能，并巩固其在尼日利亚农业价值链中的地位。N80 billion发行所得款项将用于满足季节性营运资金需求，尤其是当前经营周期内采购和加工可可及其他农产品。公司表示，这笔资金将使其能够在关键季节性时段确保原材料供应，维持旗下加工设施的运营，并保障其采购、加工和装运商品活动持续进行。集团董事总经理John Alamu在谈及这一进展时表示，超额认购充分表明投资者对公司连接农业与工业、出口和消费市场这一愿景充满信心。他说：“本次发行的反响是对Johnvents所建设事业的重要信心投票，即打造一家将农业与工业、出口和日常消费品相连接的尼日利亚企业。“我们的目标是在当地创造更多价值，并打造一家具备跨市场竞争能力的公司。这份信心也使我们肩负起严格履约的责任。”Alamu向投资者保证，所得款项将按照获批的发售文件使用，公司也将继续专注于流动性管理和按时履行还款义务。集团资金主管Samuel Olaifa表示，此次成功发行以及第21期商业票据在到期时全额赎回，反映出公司在管理融资需求和还款义务方面采取的审慎策略。他解释道，这些交易围绕公司的季节性营运资金周期设计，尤其涉及可可及其他农产品的采购、加工和装运。公司披露，此次交易之前开展了广泛的投资者沟通活动，包括管理层会议以及对Johnvents部分设施的参观，使投资者能够评估公司的运营情况、加工产能、库存周期和一体化价值链。Regius Capital代理董事总经理Kayode Omosebi表示，这些沟通活动让投资者更清楚地了解公司运营资产、库存周期、现金创造能力和偿付能力之间的关系。他指出，超额认购既反映了机构投资者对结构设计完善的信贷机会的兴趣，也凸显了公司与投资者之间开展透明沟通的重要性。公司表示，下一阶段增长将重点关注提高加工吞吐量、改善产能利用率、向更高附加值的消费品领域拓展，以及加强国内分销和出口合作关系。他补充称，其扩张战略旨在 strengthening 尼日利亚非石油出口基础、创造就业机会，并支持其农户、聚合商、运输商、分销商和服务提供商网络中的各类企业。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创刊，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕Creek Road 35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都直辖区以及世界各地设有办公室。作为尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，THISDAY通过所有平台为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级提供新闻，同时充当抱负者、千禧一代探索新思想、文化和技术的交汇点。这份报纸是一项公共信托，致力于追求真相与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育、社区，以及人与社会交叉领域的各类议题。您可以发送电子邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/s.body: Environmental stakeholders in the Niger Delta have urged Nigerians to demand concrete climate change and energy transition policies from political candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections. Executive Director of the Global Initiative for Food Security and Ecosystem Preservation (GIFSEP), Dr. Michael David, said Nigerians needed to unite to demand policies that addressed climate change, food insecurity and energy poverty. David said the 2027 election campaigns should focus on candidates’ plans to build climate resilience and ensure access to affordable, clean energy rather than being dominated by ethnic, religious and regional considerations. He said vulnerable Nigerians struggling to meet basic needs often found it difficult to organise collectively, stressing that environmental protection and access to clean energy affected everyone. According to him, Nigeria risks accumulating stranded fossil fuel assets as the world transitions to cleaner energy, while communities continue to suffer pollution from oil and coal operations. David said the country already had policies, including the Climate Change Act and Just Transition Policy, but implementation remained weak, particularly at state and local government levels. He urged state governments to utilise the Electricity Act, which empowers them to generate, transmit and distribute electricity, to expand access to clean energy. The GIFSEP executive director also called for increased investment in clean cooking solutions, noting that the high cost of gas forced many households to rely on firewood and charcoal, exposing women to harmful pollution. Coordinator of the Africa Just Transition Network, Mr. Friday Nbani, said the organisation was working with community groups and civil society organisations to address gas flaring, coal mining and other activities contributing to climate change. Nbani said the network, which had 88 member organisations across 28 African countries, would develop a roadmap for engaging government on environmental protection and a fair energy transition. He said community awareness and education were essential to ensuring that the transition did not undermine livelihoods, adding that the network would advocate increased investment in renewable energy and climate finance. Also speaking, Co-lead of the Africa Just Transition Network in Nigeria, Dr. Stella Amanie urged government to ensure that energy transition policies were affordable, inclusive and gradual, particularly for women and vulnerable communities. Amanie, who is also Executive Director of the Society for Women and Youth Affairs, said communities must be carried along in the transition to cleaner energy to prevent further hardship. A participant from Benue, Agernor Torkuma, said growing adoption of solar energy in Nigerian homes demonstrated the potential of renewable energy, but called for measures to address affordability concerns and the country’s dependence on crude oil revenue. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/s.title_zh: 利益相关方要求在2027年选举活动中纳入气候政策
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/s.body_zh: 尼日利亚三角洲的环境利益相关人士敦促尼日利亚民众，在2027年大选前要求政治候选人提出切实可行的气候变化和能源转型政策。全球粮食安全与生态系统保护倡议组织（GIFSEP）执行主任迈克尔·戴维博士表示，尼日利亚人需要团结起来，要求政策应对气候变化、粮食不安全问题和能源贫困。戴维说，2027年选举竞选活动应聚焦候选人建设气候适应能力和确保人们获得可负担清洁能源的计划，而不应被族群、宗教和地区因素主导。他说，难以满足基本生活需求的脆弱尼日利亚人往往发现很难集体组织起来，同时强调，保护环境和获得清洁能源关系到每个人。据他表示，随着世界向更清洁的能源转型，尼日利亚可能面临化石燃料资产搁浅的风险，而各地社区仍继续承受石油和煤炭作业造成的污染。戴维说，该国已经制定包括《气候变化法》和《公正转型政策》在内的政策，但落实仍然薄弱，尤其是在州和地方政府层面。他敦促各州政府利用《电力法》授予其发电、输电和配电的权力，扩大清洁能源的可及性。GIFSEP执行主任还呼吁增加对清洁烹饪解决方案的投入，并指出高昂的燃气价格迫使许多家庭依赖木柴和木炭，使妇女暴露于有害污染之中。非洲公正转型网络协调员弗赖迪·恩巴尼先生表示，该组织正与社区团体和公民社会组织开展合作，处理天然气火炬燃烧、煤炭开采及其他加剧气候变化的活动。恩巴尼说，该网络在非洲28个国家拥有88个成员组织，将制定一份路线图，就环境保护和公正能源转型与政府开展沟通。他说，提高社区认知和加强教育对于确保转型不会破坏生计至关重要，该网络还将倡导增加对可再生能源和气候融资的投入。非洲公正转型网络尼日利亚联合负责人斯特拉·阿马妮博士也发言敦促政府，确保能源转型政策价格可负担、具有包容性且循序渐进，尤其要照顾妇女和脆弱社区。阿马妮还是妇女与青年事务协会执行主任，她说，必须让社区参与向更清洁能源转型的过程，以防进一步加剧困难。来自贝努埃州的活动参与者阿格尔诺尔·托库马表示，太阳能日益被尼日利亚家庭采用，证明了可再生能源的潜力，但呼吁采取措施解决可负担性问题以及该国对原油收入的依赖。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创刊，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，社址位于尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕溪路35号，并在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区及世界各地设有办公室。它是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，通过所有平台为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶层提供服务，同时作为抱有志向者和千禧一代的新思想、文化与技术交汇点。该报秉持公众信任， dedicated于追求真相与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育和社区等议题，直面人与社会的交汇点。您可以发送电子邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

The initiative reflected an effort by the candidate’s mobilisers to build a wider grassroots network across the four states and connect with voters at the community level. By taking the campaign into remote settlements and areas described by the organisers as ungoverned, the mobilisation sought to bring political engagement to communities that frequently experienced limited government presence and inadequate public services. The outreach was part of a broader North-west mobilisation strategy associated with a six-million-vote target announced by the Hashim Progressive Movement. The target covers all seven states in the region: Kano, Katsina, Kaduna, Jigawa, Kebbi, Sokoto, and Zamfara. The focus on Kano, Katsina, Kaduna, and Jigawa gave the current rural initiative a strategic regional dimension. It placed particular emphasis on building support in states with substantial voting populations, while extending the campaign’s reach into communities beyond the main urban centres. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/p.body: The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has fixed December 10, 2026, as the deadline for the submission of nominations for party agents ahead of the 2027 general elections. It urged its state chapters to ensure the timely registration and uploading of their agents on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) portal. The party said the deadline was aimed at preventing last-minute challenges associated with the registration of agents and ensuring that only loyal, committed and properly vetted members were nominated to represent it at polling units across the country. The National Organising Secretary of the PDP, Umar Bature, announced the deadline on Monday in Abuja during a one-day INEC portal capacity-building and training programme organised for state secretaries, state organising secretaries and state information and communication technology (ICT) officers. Bature said the training was designed to equip party officials with the technical knowledge required to upload agents’ details to the INEC portal, stressing that the process was critical to the party’s preparations for the forthcoming elections. He disclosed that the programme was attended by eight state secretaries, 21 state organising secretaries and 25 ICT officers. According to him, the successful registration of party agents was essential to effective election monitoring, particularly as the party had recently faced challenges relating to the uploading of candidates on the INEC portal. “We have just finished the battle with INEC over the uploading of candidates, and you can see that INEC is doing whatever it wants to do, particularly after the Supreme Court judgment,” he said. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/p.title_zh: 人民民主党为提交投票站代理人设定12月10日最后期限
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/p.body_zh:
人民民主党（PDP）已将2026年12月10日确定为2027年大选前提交党内代理人提名的截止日期。该党敦促各州分部确保及时在独立国家选举委员会（INEC）门户网站登记并上传代理人信息。该党表示，设定这一截止日期旨在防止代理人登记相关问题在最后关头才出现，并确保只有忠诚、坚定且经过适当审查的成员获提名，代表该党在全国各投票站工作。

PDP全国组织秘书Umar Bature于周日在阿布贾举行的为期一天的INEC门户网站能力建设和培训活动上宣布了这一截止日期。该活动面向州秘书、州组织秘书以及州信息与通信技术（ICT）官员举行。Bature表示，此次培训旨在使党内官员掌握将代理人详细信息上传至INEC门户网站所需的技术知识，并强调这一流程对该党筹备即将举行的大选至关重要。他透露，共有8名州秘书、21名州组织秘书和25名ICT官员参加了此次活动。

据他介绍，成功登记党内代理人是有效监督选举的关键，尤其是该党近期在INEC门户网站上传候选人时曾遇到问题。他说：“我们刚刚结束了与INEC围绕候选人上传问题的较量。你们可以看到，在最高法院作出裁决后，INEC想怎么做就怎么做。”

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/m.summary: Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, yesterday, inaugurated the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council for the 2027 general election, urging members to conduct a peaceful, issue-based and disciplined campaign towards securing victory for President Bola Tinubu, Vice President Kashim Shettima and all APC candidates in the state.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/m.summary_zh: Plateau州州长Caleb Mutfwang昨日为2027年大选成立全进步大会党（APC）竞选委员会，并敦促成员开展和平、以议题为导向且恪守纪律的竞选活动，争取让总统Bola Tinubu、副总统Kashim Shettima以及该州所有APC候选人获胜。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/m.body: Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, yesterday, inaugurated the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council for the 2027 general election, urging members to conduct a peaceful, issue-based and disciplined campaign towards securing victory for President Bola Tinubu, Vice President Kashim Shettima and all APC candidates in the state. Speaking at the inauguration held at Government House, Rayfield, Jos, Mutfwang said his administration had recorded progress in key sectors and deserved another term to consolidate ongoing projects and programmes. The governor reaffirmed his commitment to tackling insecurity, disclosing plans to facilitate the return of internally displaced persons, deploy 800 trained forest guards and commission another batch of retrained Operation Rainbow personnel to strengthen security across vulnerable communities. He also defended the economic reforms of the Tinubu administration, saying the country required time to recover from longstanding fiscal challenges, while highlighting state interventions such as Tin City Metro buses, revived rail services, reduced tuition fees and increased student allowances. Calling for party unity, Mutfwang urged campaign council members to intensify grassroots mobilisation, stressing that electoral victories were won at polling units and not in political centres. Earlier, the Director-General of the Mutfwang/Piyo 2027 Governorship Campaign Council, Sir Joseph Ari, pledged a disciplined, issue-based and inclusive campaign, revealing that 115 support groups had already indicated support for the project. Ari commended the administration’s “Time Is Now” policy direction, particularly its emphasis on unity, mutual respect and development, describing peaceful coexistence as indispensable to sustainable progress in Plateau State. Also, Plateau APC Chairman, Rufus Bature, described the inauguration as a major step towards building a formidable structure for the 2027 elections and charged council members to work diligently to ensure the party’s success. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/2.title_zh: 2027：埃格巴集团拒绝独立国家选举委员会据称选择性执行最高法院裁决
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/2.body_zh:
埃格巴诚信组织（EIG）谴责独立国家选举委员会（INEC）选择性执法。10月29日星期四委员会召开会议后，该组织指责INEC在执法过程中标准不一。

该组织表示，INEC执行了最高法院关于州长候选人所属政党党员名册提交期限的裁决，却拒绝在奥贡州国民议会候选人案中采取同样措施。它补充道：“最高法院于2026年9月24日在INEC诉ZLP一案（SC/CV/495/2026）中裁定，《2026年选举法》第77(5)(6)(7)条具有强制性。”

该组织坚持认为，INEC在10月29日采取了选择性执法。它表示：“对于州长候选人：INEC严格执行规定——Isa Pantami（贡贝州PDP）——有条件获准参选；Abdulsalam Gwarzo（卡诺州NDC）——有条件获准参选；Ladi Adebutu（奥贡州PDP州长候选人）——被拒。

“INEC称‘奥贡州PDP候选人未能通过审核。’对于国民议会候选人，INEC拒绝执行相同规定。PDP在奥贡州提交的名册存在缺陷，并因此导致Adebutu被取消资格，但该名册却被用来保留Iyabo Obasanjo参议员（奥贡州中部PDP）及其他国民议会候选人的资格。这属于非法歧视。

“第77条并未区分州长和参议员。名册只有一份。如果该名册对州长候选人无效，那么对参议员候选人同样无效。”

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/a.summary: Presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has condemned President Bola Tinubu for allegedly abandoning retired police officers to a broken pension system and forcing them to fight for the dignity and security they earned through years of service. Atiku said a government that could deploy police officers to protect the powerful but could not protect them in retirement had failed them utterly.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/a.summary_zh: 非洲民主大会（ADC）总统候选人Atiku Abubakar谴责总统Bola Tinubu，指其涉嫌将退休警察抛入陷入困境的养老金体系，迫使他们为多年服役所赢得的尊严和安全而抗争。Atiku表示，一个能够派遣警察保护权势者、却无法在他们退休后保护他们的政府，已经彻底辜负了他们。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/a.body: Presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has condemned President Bola Tinubu for allegedly abandoning retired police officers to a broken pension system and forcing them to fight for the dignity and security they earned through years of service. In a statement issued by Director of Strategic Communication of ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said it was disgraceful that officers, who risked their lives protecting Nigerians had been reduced to staging daily protests at the National Pension Commission simply to make their legitimate demands heard. Atiku said a government that could deploy police officers to protect the powerful but could not protect them in retirement had failed them utterly. He stated that the administration’s treatment of retired officers exposed the hollowness of its claims to be tackling insecurity. Atiku said he was deeply troubled by the protests and had instructed his team to meet with the officers and hear their concerns directly. He also faulted Tinubu for failing to act on the Police Exit Bill, which, according to the statement, had remained on his desk since March. The ADC candidate condemned the government’s “use and discard” treatment of officers, who spent their careers protecting Nigerians, including political office holders, only to be abandoned when they needed support most. Atiku said his Police Dignity Guarantee Plan would put the welfare and retirement security of law enforcement officers at the centre of his approach to tackling insecurity. The plan included prompt action on the Police Exit Bill, restoring gratuity for police officers, and ensuring that officers were treated with dignity both during service and in retirement. He also pledged to implement the Police Pension Board Bill within 30 days of taking office. Atiku said, “Insecurity cannot be defeated while those who protect the country are denied security in retirement. “My Police Dignity Guarantee Plan will ensure that officers who serve Nigeria are properly supported throughout their careers and are not abandoned when they retire. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/a.body_zh: 非洲民主大会党（ADC）总统候选人阿蒂库·阿布巴卡尔谴责总统博拉·蒂努布，指控他遗弃已退休的警察，任由他们被抛入陷入瘫痪的养老金体系，并迫使他们为维护自己通过多年服役所赢得的尊严与保障而抗争。ADC总统竞选委员会战略传播主任弗兰克·沙伊布发表声明称，阿蒂库说，那些冒着生命危险保护尼日利亚人的警员如今每天到国家养老金委员会门前示威，只为让自己的正当诉求得到倾听，这是可耻的。阿蒂库表示，一个政府若能派遣警察保护权势者，却无法在他们退休后保护他们，就已彻底辜负了他们。他说，政府对待退休警员的方式，暴露了其打击不安全问题的说法何等空洞。阿蒂库表示，他对这些抗议深感不安，并已指示团队与警员会面，直接听取他们的关切。他还指责蒂努布未能推动《警察离职法案》落地；根据声明，该法案自3月以来一直搁置在他的办公桌上。这名ADC候选人谴责政府对警员“利用后抛弃”的做法。警员一生都在保护尼日利亚人，包括政治职位担任者，却在最需要支持时被遗弃。阿蒂库表示，他的《警察尊严保障计划》将以执法人员的福祉和退休保障为核心，推动解决不安全问题。该计划包括迅速落实《警察离职法案》、恢复警察应享的退休酬劳，以及确保警员在职期间和退休后都能受到有尊严的对待。他还承诺，上任30天内将实施《警察养老金委员会法案》。阿蒂库说：“如果那些保护国家的人退休后仍被剥夺保障，就不可能击败不安全问题。”“我的《警察尊严保障计划》将确保为尼日利亚服务的警员在其整个职业生涯中得到适当支持，不会在退休时被遗弃。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创刊，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区及世界各地设有办公室。作为尼日利亚最权威的新闻媒体，THISDAY通过所有平台为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级提供服务，同时充当有志者、千禧一代与新思想、文化和技术的交汇点。该报是一项公共信托，致力于追求真相与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育和社区，以及人与社会的交叉领域。您可以发送电子邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/g.summary: The 2001 set of Government Secondary School (GSS), Kuje, Abuja, yesterday donated water facilities, rehabilitated the school’s solar power system and provided furniture for its robotics laboratory to improve students’ welfare and promote technology education. Chairman of the alumni set, Ahmed Zakari, said the initiative was designed to make a lasting contribution to the school that shaped the lives and careers of its members.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/g.summary_zh: 2001届政府中学（GSS）库杰分校位于阿布贾，昨天捐建了供水设施，翻修了学校的太阳能供电系统，并为机器人实验室配备了家具，以改善学生福利并推动技术教育。校友会主席艾哈迈德·扎卡里表示，此项举措旨在为这所学校作出持久贡献；该校曾塑造其成员的人生轨迹和职业发展。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/g.body: The 2001 set of Government Secondary School (GSS), Kuje, Abuja, yesterday donated water facilities, rehabilitated the school’s solar power system and provided furniture for its robotics laboratory to improve students’ welfare and promote technology education. The projects were commissioned during the set’s 25th anniversary celebration as part of efforts to give back to the institution and improve its teaching and learning environment. Chairman of the alumni set, Ahmed Zakari, said the initiative was designed to make a lasting contribution to the school that shaped the lives and careers of its members. Zakari said the interventions included maintenance of the school’s solar power system, installation of a water tank at the boys’ hostel and extension of borehole water supply to the girls’ hostel. He added that the set provided tables and chairs for the robotics laboratory to encourage practical learning and expose students to technology and innovation. “We wanted our 25th anniversary to mean something. We wanted to return to the school that helped shape us and leave behind something that would benefit those coming after us,” he said. He explained that although the projects might not address all the challenges facing the school, they represented a significant step towards improving students’ welfare and educational experience. Zakari also disclosed that former teachers and administrative staff who served the institution were recognised with cash donations and bags of rice. He urged other alumni sets to emulate the initiative, stressing that collective contributions could transform the school. Similarly, a member of the set’s Fundraising Committee, Onyeka Ofodile, said the projects were inspired by the desire to give back to an institution that contributed significantly to their personal and professional development. Ofodile said members had pursued different careers and attributed part of their achievements to the education and values acquired at GSS Kuje. He expressed satisfaction with the school’s development, noting improvements in its infrastructure and learning environment since their graduation. Also speaking, the set’s Head Boy, Abubakar Ibrahim, described the teachers as builders whose discipline, guidance and commitment had shaped the lives of the alumni. He urged current students to take their studies seriously, respect their teachers and remain disciplined, noting that their experiences in school would influence their future. Similarly, the set’s Head Girl, Grace Nehemiah, commended the teachers for their sacrifices, including using personal resources to support students when teaching materials were inadequate. Nehemiah urged the students to cherish their school, obey their teachers and strive to become worthy ambassadors of the institution. The Principal of GSS Kuje, Adam Bello-Gupa, represented by the Vice Principal, Administration, Margaret Agbugba, appreciated the alumni for their contributions, saying the projects would support teaching and learning. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/g.body_zh: 2001届政府中学（GSS）校友会昨日向位于阿布贾库杰的政府中学捐赠供水设施，翻修学校太阳能供电系统，并为学校机器人实验室提供家具，以改善学生福利、推动技术教育。这些项目在该届校友会成立25周年庆祝活动期间正式启用，旨在回馈学校并改善其教学和学习环境。校友会主席艾哈迈德·扎卡里表示，该项举措旨在为曾塑造其成员人生与职业道路的学校作出持久贡献。扎卡里说，相关干预措施包括维护学校太阳能供电系统、在男生宿舍安装储水罐，并将钻井供水延伸至女生宿舍。他还补充说，该届校友会为机器人实验室提供了桌椅，以鼓励实践学习，让学生接触技术与创新。扎卡里说：“我们希望25周年具有实际意义。我们希望回到曾经帮助塑造我们的学校，并留下一些能让后来者受益的东西。”他解释道，尽管这些项目未必能解决学校面临的所有挑战，但它们代表着改善学生福利和教育体验的重要一步。扎卡里还披露，曾在该校任职的往届教师和行政人员均获赠现金及一袋袋大米作为表彰。他敦促其他届校友会效仿这一举措，强调集体 donations 能够改变学校面貌。同样，该届校友会筹款委员会成员奥尼耶卡·奥福利勒表示，这些项目源于回馈曾对其个人和职业发展作出重大贡献的学校的愿望。奥福利勒说，成员们各自走上了不同的职业道路，并将部分成就归功于在库杰政府中学接受的教育和汲取的价值观。他对学校的发展表示满意，并指出自他们毕业以来，学校基础设施和学习环境均有改善。该届校友会男生代表阿布巴卡·易卜拉欣也发言称，教师们的纪律、指导和投入塑造了校友们的人生，是建设学校栋梁。他敦促在校学生认真学习、尊重教师并保持自律，指出在校经历将影响他们的未来。同样，该届校友会女生代表格蕾丝·尼希米亚赞扬教师们的牺牲精神，包括在教学材料不足时动用个人资源支持学生。尼希米亚敦促学生珍惜学校、服从师长，并努力成为学校的合格使者。库杰政府中学校长亚当·贝洛－古帕由行政副校长玛格丽特·阿格布巴代为出席。玛格丽特·阿格布巴感谢校友们的贡献，并表示这些项目将为教学和学习提供支持。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创办，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，社址位于尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕溪路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区及世界各地设有办公室。该报是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，通过所有平台为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶层服务，同时充当有抱负者和千禧一代探索新思想、文化与技术的交汇点。这份报纸承载公众信任，致力于追求真相与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育和社区等议题，直至探讨人与社会的交汇点。您可以发送邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/f.title: Femicide: NHRC, AU Rights Envoy Mount Pressure on Nigeria to Ratify Convention
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/f.summary: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) and the African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights have stepped up pressure on Nigeria to ratify the African Union Convention on Ending Violence Against Women and Girls, amid growing concerns over femicide, sexual violence and the increasing use of digital platforms to intimidate women.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/f.summary_zh: 在杀害女性、性暴力以及利用数字平台恐吓女性的现象日益受到关注的背景下，国家人权委员会和非洲人权与人民权利委员会加大了对尼日利亚的压力，敦促其批准《非洲联盟制止针对妇女和女童暴力行为公约》。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/f.body: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) and the African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights have stepped up pressure on Nigeria to ratify the African Union Convention on Ending Violence Against Women and Girls, amid growing concerns over femicide, sexual violence and the increasing use of digital platforms to intimidate women. The push which comes ahead of the 2027 general elections also includes demands for affirmative action and reserved seats for women in parliament to address persistent barriers to their political representation. The Executive Secretary of the NHRC, Tony Ojukwu, gave the commitment during an advocacy meeting with the African Commission’s Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Women in Africa, Hon. Janet Ramatoulie Sallah-Njie, at the commission’s headquarters. The proposed ratification would commit Nigeria to a stronger regional framework for preventing and addressing violence against women and girls, including femicide, while strengthening accountability and protection mechanisms. Ojukwu said the NHRC would mobilise civil society organisations and other stakeholders to intensify advocacy for Nigeria’s adoption and ratification of the instrument, assuring that the commission would pursue concrete actions rather than allow the engagement to end with expressions of commitment. He said observations by the African Commission on Nigeria’s human rights reports had highlighted troubling developments, particularly femicide and technology-facilitated violence against women, requiring stronger legislative, institutional and enforcement responses. The NHRC boss said the commission would also work with relevant institutions to improve access to justice for victims of gender-based violence and ensure that recommendations from the African Commission were implemented. The urgency of the campaign was underscored by Sallah-Njie, who challenged Nigeria to use its continental influence to help secure the entry into force of the convention by becoming one of the 15 countries required to facilitate its implementation. She disclosed that the African Union adopted the convention in February 2025, describing it as a significant addition to existing continental human rights protections because of its response to emerging forms of violence against women and girls. According to her, Nigeria’s ratification would demonstrate its commitment to protecting women and girls while strengthening the continent’s collective response to gender-based violence. She expressed concern over femicide in Nigeria, alongside developments in Cameroon and South Africa, and called on the NHRC to champion the ratification campaign, prepare relevant national reports and monitor the implementation of laws protecting women and girls. Sallah-Njie particularly highlighted the importance of the convention’s explicit recognition and prohibition of femicide, arguing that stronger legal recognition was necessary to confront the killing of women because of their gender. But beyond the ratification campaign, the visiting envoy raised another major concern: the exclusion of women from political decision-making and the violence increasingly accompanying their participation in electoral activities. With the 2027 elections approaching, she called for temporary special measures, including affirmative action and reserved seats for women in parliament, arguing that granting women the right to contest elections was insufficient without measures to overcome structural and socio-cultural disadvantages. She said women continued to face barriers that prevented them from competing on equal terms with men, insisting that deliberate interventions were necessary to translate formal political rights into meaningful representation. The Special Rapporteur urged Nigerian women to scrutinise the voting records of their representatives on legislation affecting women’s rights and hold them accountable, while encouraging more women to contest elective positions. She also warned that attacks, intimidation and victimisation of women pursuing political ambitions could discourage others from seeking public office. Of particular concern, she identified election-related sexual violence, harassment and technology-facilitated abuse as threats capable of pushing women out of the political space. She urged the NHRC and other relevant authorities to monitor such violations and establish preventive mechanisms to ensure that women could campaign, vote and contest elections without fear of violence or discrimination. Sallah-Njie further called for women’s inclusion in peacebuilding and conflict-resolution processes, maintaining that decisions on security and the future of communities must not exclude half of the population. Responding to the concerns, Ojukwu disclosed that the NHRC had established thematic departments, including a dedicated Department of Women and Children, to strengthen its response to violations affecting vulnerable groups. He said the restructuring was intended to provide specialised attention to human rights concerns rather than rely solely on a general institutional approach. He also highlighted the commission’s collaboration with the African Commission, noting that regional resolutions and recommendations were important in strengthening Nigeria’s human rights protection framework. The NHRC, he added, had linked its website with that of the African Commission to make relevant human rights instruments, resolutions and recommendations more accessible to Nigerians seeking information and remedies. The Executive Director of Baobab for Women’s Human Rights, Yèyé Bunmi Dipo-Salami, supported the call for affirmative action, recalling previous advocacy for special seats for women in the National Assembly. She said the proposal had faced resistance from some lawmakers who argued that reserving seats for women would discriminate against men. Dipo-Salami, however, maintained that affirmative action was an internationally recognised mechanism for addressing historical inequalities and ensuring meaningful representation of disadvantaged groups. She commended the NHRC for creating specialised departments and providing leadership opportunities for women, while pledging civil society support for efforts to advance gender equality. The delegation also included representatives of the Women’s Advocacy Research and Documentation Centre (WARDC), among other stakeholders. Sallah-Njie said she would report the outcome of the engagement in her next intersessional report to the African human rights community, expressing hope that Nigeria would demonstrate measurable progress in ratifying and implementing the convention. She said tangible action by Nigeria would strengthen the continent’s efforts to end violence against women and girls. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/f.title_zh: 女性杀害问题：国家人权委员会和非盟人权特使敦促尼日利亚批准相关公约
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/f.body_zh: 国家人权委员会（NHRC）和非洲人权与人民权利委员会加大压力，要求尼日利亚批准《非洲联盟终止对妇女和女童暴力行为公约》。在针对杀害女性、性暴力以及利用数字平台恐吓女性的现象日益令人担忧之际，这项推动工作正值2027年大选前展开，还要求采取平权行动并在议会为女性保留席位，以解决女性在政治代表方面长期面临的障碍。NHRC执行秘书Tony Ojukwu在非洲委员会总部与该委员会非洲妇女权利特别报告员Hon. Janet Ramatoulie Sallah-Njie举行倡导会议时，作出了这一承诺。拟议中的批准将促使尼日利亚承诺采取更有力的区域框架，预防并处理针对妇女和女童的暴力行为，包括杀害女性，同时加强问责和保护机制。Ojukwu表示，NHRC将动员民间社会组织及其他利益相关方，加强对推动尼日利亚通过并批准该文书的倡导力度，并保证委员会将采取具体行动，避免让此次接触仅以口头承诺告终。他说，非洲委员会对尼日利亚人权报告提出的意见凸显了令人不安的进展，尤其是杀害女性以及利用技术实施的针对女性的暴力行为，因此需要采取更有力的立法、制度和执法措施。NHRC负责人表示，委员会还将与相关机构合作，改善基于性别的暴力受害者的司法可及性，并确保落实非洲委员会的建议。Sallah-Njie强调了这项运动的紧迫性，呼吁尼日利亚利用其大陆影响力，通过成为推动公约实施所需的15个国家之一，帮助促成公约正式生效。她透露，非洲联盟于2025年2月通过了该公约，并称该公约针对新出现的针对妇女和女童的暴力形式作出回应，是对现有大陆人权保护的重要补充。据她表示，尼日利亚批准该公约将展现其保护妇女和女童的决心，同时加强非洲大陆对基于性别的暴力的集体应对。她对尼日利亚以及喀麦隆和南非出现的杀害女性现象表示关切，并呼吁NHRC推动批准工作、编制相关国家报告并监督保护妇女和女童的法律的实施情况。Sallah-Njie尤其强调，公约明确承认并禁止杀害女性具有重要意义；她认为，必须加强法律层面的承认，才能应对女性因其性别而遭到杀害的问题。但除了推动批准外，这位来访特使还提出了另一项重大关切：女性被排除在政治决策之外，以及女性参与选举活动时日益伴随的暴力行为。随着2027年大选临近，她呼吁采取临时特别措施，包括平权行动和在议会为女性保留席位，并认为如果不采取措施克服结构性和社会文化方面的劣势，仅赋予女性参选权仍远远不够。她说，女性继续面临阻碍其与男性平等竞争的障碍，坚持必须通过有意的干预措施，才能将形式上的政治权利转化为切实的政治代表性。这位特别报告员敦促尼日利亚女性审查其代表在涉及妇女权利的立法方面的投票记录，并追究其责任，同时鼓励更多女性竞选公职。她还警告，追逐政治抱负的女性遭受袭击、恐吓和迫害，可能使其他人不敢寻求公职。她尤其担心与选举有关的性暴力、骚扰以及利用技术实施的虐待，这些威胁可能迫使女性退出政治领域。她敦促NHRC及其他相关当局监测此类违法行为，并建立预防机制，确保女性能够开展竞选、投票和参选，而不必担心暴力或歧视。Sallah-Njie还呼吁让女性参与建设和平与解决冲突的进程，强调有关安全和社区未来的决策不得将占人口一半的女性排除在外。针对这些关切，Ojukwu透露，NHRC已经设立多个专项部门，其中包括专门的妇女与儿童部，以加强对影响弱势群体的侵权行为的应对。他说，此次重组旨在让人权问题得到专业处理，而不是仅仅依赖综合性的机构工作方法。他还介绍了委员会与非洲委员会之间的合作，指出区域决议和建议对于加强尼日利亚人权保护框架十分重要。他补充说，NHRC已将其网站与非洲委员会的网站链接起来，使寻求信息和救济的尼日利亚人更容易获取相关人权文书、决议和建议。Baobab for Women’s Human Rights执行主任Yèyé Bunmi Dipo-Salami支持采取平权行动的呼吁，并回顾了此前为全国议会女性设置特别席位所做的倡导工作。她说，该提议曾遭到一些议员反对，他们认为为女性保留席位会对男性构成歧视。然而，Dipo-Salami坚持认为，平权行动是国际公认的机制，可用于处理历史不平等并确保弱势群体获得切实的政治代表性。她赞扬NHRC设立专项部门并为女性提供领导岗位的机会，同时承诺民间社会将支持推动性别平等的努力。代表团成员还包括妇女倡导研究与文献中心（WARDC）的代表，以及其他利益相关方。Sallah-Njie表示，她将在下一份提交给非洲人权界的休会期报告中汇报此次接触的结果，并希望尼日利亚在批准和实施该公约方面取得可衡量的进展。她说，尼日利亚采取切实行动将加强非洲大陆终结针对妇女和女童暴力行为的努力。THISDAY创刊于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY A statement said the delegation engaged with senior executives of Dangote Group to identify areas for industrial collaboration, investment partnerships, and capacity expansion across key sectors.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/d.summary_zh: 丹格特集团正在探索将其工业投资扩大至埃及的机会，此举可能成为其泛非增长战略的重要里程碑，并深化尼日利亚与埃及之间的经济联系。一份声明称，该代表团与丹格特集团的高层管理人员进行了磋商，以确定在重点领域开展工业合作、建立投资伙伴关系和扩大产能的领域。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/d.body: Dangote Group is exploring opportunities to expand its industrial investments into Egypt, a move that could mark a significant milestone in its pan-African growth strategy and deepen economic ties between Nigeria and Egypt. The development follows a visit by a high-level Egyptian delegation led by that country’s Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade, Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh, to the Dangote Industries complex in Lagos. A statement said the delegation engaged with senior executives of Dangote Group to identify areas for industrial collaboration, investment partnerships, and capacity expansion across key sectors. Accompanied by officials from Egypt’s Ministry of Petroleum and senior executives from the country’s oil and petrochemical industry, the delegation explored opportunities for Nigerian and Egyptian businesses to establish mutually beneficial ventures, leveraging the strengths of both economies. The visit underscores growing interest in extending Nigeria’s industrial expertise across the continent, with Egypt emerging as a potential destination for future Dangote investments as the group advances its Vision 2030 expansion agenda. President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, described the visit as a powerful symbol of African economic integration and a reflection of the group’s commitment to driving industrialisation across the continent. Dangote stated, “This demonstrates true African integration. It reflects our belief that African businesses must invest across the continent to accelerate industrialisation and economic development. We are proud to be an African company building industries that create value for Africa.” He said the Egyptian delegation’s visit provided an opportunity to showcase the scale of industrial development achieved by the group while identifying avenues for collaboration that could strengthen industrial capacity in both countries. According to Dangote, the engagement represents a broader effort to foster partnerships among African businesses and unlock new opportunities for sustainable industrial growth. Speaking during the visit, Saleh said the mission was aimed at translating ongoing diplomatic and business engagements between Nigeria and Egypt into concrete investment opportunities and industrial partnerships. He explained that the visit followed previous interactions involving Dangote Group at the Alamein Economic Conference and other international investment forums hosted by Egypt. The minister said Egypt was particularly interested in understanding the industrial capabilities developed by Dangote Group in refining, petrochemicals, fertiliser production, and related manufacturing activities, with a view to exploring collaborative opportunities. Saleh said, “We are impressed by the scale of operations we have seen here—from refining and petrochemicals to fertiliser production. Our objective is to identify areas where Egyptian and Nigerian businesses can collaborate, expand industrial capacities, and create long-term value for both economies.” He stressed that stronger private-sector collaboration would be critical to unlocking the full potential of economic relations between both countries. Saleh stated, “The private sector must be at the centre of this partnership. By learning from each other’s experiences and combining our strengths, we can expand industrial production, encourage investment flows, and create sustainable growth opportunities for our people.” Saleh highlighted the enormous opportunities presented by the combined market of approximately 400 million people in Nigeria and Egypt, stating that both countries possess complementary strengths capable of driving industrial expansion across Africa. According to him, Nigeria’s vast energy resources and Egypt’s established industrial base provide a strong foundation for deeper cooperation in manufacturing, energy, petrochemicals, fertilisers, and other strategic sectors. He added that stronger collaboration could encourage Nigerian industrialists to expand into Egypt, while creating opportunities for Egyptian businesses to strengthen their presence in Nigeria, fostering a mutually beneficial investment ecosystem. The minister stated that the benefits of such cooperation would go beyond trade and investment, extending to job creation, technology transfer, skills development, and the emergence of supporting industries. Asked whether Egypt would welcome a Dangote refinery investment, Saleh indicated that the scope of potential collaboration was much broader. He stated, “It doesn’t have to be a refinery specifically. There are several sectors in which collaboration can happen. What is important is building a partnership that creates value for both countries and for Africa as a whole.” The engagement aligns with Dangote Group’s broader Vision 2030 strategy, which seeks to expand the company’s industrial footprint across Africa, strengthen regional value chains, and position the continent as a globally competitive manufacturing hub. Beyond refining and petrochemicals, the evolving relationship between Nigerian and Egyptian industrial players is expected to open opportunities in fertiliser production, manufacturing, energy-related investments, and industrial services. As both countries pursue higher levels of industrialisation, private-sector growth and job creation, the emerging partnership could become a model for mobilising African capital, expertise, and industrial capacity in support of a more integrated and prosperous continent. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/d.title_zh: 随着埃及探索投资机会，桑戈洛将目光投向非洲工业扩张下一阶段
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/d.body_zh: 丹格特集团正在探索将其工业投资扩大至埃及的机会，这一举措可能成为其泛非增长战略的重要里程碑，并深化尼日利亚与埃及之间的经济联系。此次发展源于由埃及投资与对外贸易部长穆罕默德·法里德·萨利赫博士率领的埃及高级代表团访问拉各斯的丹格特工业园区。一份声明称，代表团与丹格特集团的高层管理人员举行会谈，探讨在重点领域开展工业协作、投资伙伴关系和扩大产能。代表团成员包括埃及石油部官员以及该国石油和石化行业的高级管理人员，他们探索了尼日利亚和埃及企业建立互利合作项目的机会，利用两种经济体各自的优势。此次访问凸显了各方日益希望将尼日利亚的工业专长推广至整个非洲大陆；随着丹格特集团推进“2030愿景”扩张议程，埃及正成为其未来投资的潜在目的地。丹格特实业有限公司董事长兼首席执行官阿里科·丹格特称，此次访问是非洲经济一体化的有力象征，也体现了该集团推动非洲大陆工业化的承诺。丹格特表示：“这体现了真正的非洲一体化。它印证了我们的看法，即非洲企业必须在整个大陆投资，以加快工业化和经济发展。我们很自豪成为一家非洲公司，建设为非洲创造价值的产业。”他说，埃及代表团的访问提供了一个机会，既能展示该集团所实现的工业发展规模，也能寻找加强两国工业产能的合作途径。据丹格特介绍，此次交流是推动非洲企业建立伙伴关系、开拓可持续工业增长新机遇的更广泛努力的一部分。萨利赫在访问期间表示，此行旨在将尼日利亚与埃及持续开展的外交和商业交流转化为具体投资机会与工业伙伴关系。他解释说，此次访问是在此前丹格特集团参加阿拉明经济会议以及埃及主办的其他国际投资论坛并开展交流之后进行的。部长表示，埃及尤其希望了解丹格特集团在炼油、石化、化肥生产及相关制造活动中形成的工业能力，以探索合作机会。萨利赫说：“我们在这里看到的运营规模令人印象深刻，涵盖炼油、石化和化肥生产。我们的目标是找出埃及和尼日利亚企业可以开展协作、扩大工业产能并为两国经济创造长期价值的领域。”他强调，加强私营部门合作对于充分释放两国经济关系的潜力至关重要。萨利赫表示：“私营部门必须成为这一伙伴关系的核心。通过相互借鉴经验并结合各自优势，我们可以扩大工业生产、鼓励投资流动，并为我们的人民创造可持续增长机会。”萨利赫强调，尼日利亚和埃及合计约4亿人口的大市场带来了巨大机遇，两国拥有互补优势，能够推动非洲大陆的工业扩张。据他介绍，尼日利亚丰富的能源资源和埃及成熟的工业基础，为双方在制造业、能源、石化、化肥及其他战略领域深化合作奠定了坚实基础。他补充说，更紧密的协作可以鼓励尼日利亚实业家拓展埃及市场，同时为埃及企业加强在尼日利亚的业务布局创造机会，从而培育互利共赢的投资生态。部长表示，此类合作带来的益处将超越贸易和投资，延伸至创造就业、技术转移、技能培养以及配套产业的兴起。当被问及埃及是否欢迎丹格特投资建设炼油厂时，萨利赫表示，潜在合作的范围要广泛得多。他说：“不一定非要是炼油厂。双方可以在多个领域开展合作。重要的是建立一种伙伴关系，为两国乃至整个非洲创造价值。”此次交流与丹格特集团更宏大的“2030愿景”战略相契合。该战略旨在扩大公司的非洲工业布局、强化区域价值链，并将非洲大陆打造为全球具有竞争力的制造业中心。除炼油和石化外，尼日利亚与埃及工业参与者之间不断深化的关系预计将为化肥生产、制造业、能源相关投资和工业服务带来新的机遇。随着两国不断追求更高水平的工业化、私营部门增长和就业创造，这一新兴伙伴关系可能成为动员非洲资本、专业知识和工业能力、支持建设更加一体化且繁荣富裕的非洲大陆的典范。THISDAY创刊于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕溪路35号，并在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区及世界各地设有办公室。作为尼日利亚最权威的新闻媒体，该报通过所有平台服务政界、商业界、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶层，同时充当思想、文化和技术交汇的平台，服务于有抱负者和千禧一代。该报是一项公共信任项目，秉持追求真相与理性的宗旨，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育和社区等议题，直面人民与社会交汇的各类问题。您可以发送电子邮件至hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/a.title: Aiyedatiwa Tasks Alumni, Stakeholders to Rescue Public Schools from Infrastructure Deficit
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/a.summary: Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State has urged financially capable alumni of public schools across the country to invest in the development of their alma maters, saying the responsibility of providing quality education and adequate infrastructure should not rest solely on government.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/a.summary_zh: 奥恩多州州长Lucky Aiyedatiwa敦促全国各公校中经济条件较好的校友投资发展母校，称提供优质教育和充分基础设施的责任不应完全由政府承担。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/a.body: Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State has urged financially capable alumni of public schools across the country to invest in the development of their alma maters, saying the responsibility of providing quality education and adequate infrastructure should not rest solely on government. The governor made the appeal at the 50th anniversary celebration of Omo’luorogbo Grammar School, Akure, where he challenged old students and other stakeholders to complement government’s efforts by addressing infrastructural gaps and improving the learning environment in public schools. Aiyedatiwa, who was represented by the Commissioner for Physical Planning and Urban Development, Mr. Sunday Olajide, said meaningful contributions from alumni remained critical to sustaining educational institutions and ensuring that younger generations had access to quality learning facilities. He noted that government could not shoulder the enormous financial demands of the education sector alone, stressing that partnerships with former students, corporate organisations and other stakeholders would accelerate the development of public schools. According to him, the golden jubilee celebration offered the alumni an opportunity to demonstrate their appreciation to the institution that laid the foundation for their personal and professional achievements. He said, “Government cannot do it alone. We need the support of old students and other stakeholders to complement our efforts in providing quality education and improving infrastructure in our public schools.” The governor added that collective investment in education would help bridge existing infrastructural deficits and create a more conducive atmosphere for teaching and learning. Speaking at the event, Chairman of the 50th Anniversary Planning Committee and former Ondo State Commissioner for Information, Mr. Kayode Akinmade, said the alumni had chosen to mark the school’s golden jubilee with tangible projects that would improve its facilities and support the academic development of current students. Akinmade described giving back to the institution as a responsibility rather than an act of charity, noting that the school had provided the foundation upon which many of its former students built successful careers. He said the interventions were designed to ensure that present and future students enjoyed better learning conditions, adding that the alumni were determined to preserve the school’s legacy through sustainable investments. Among the projects executed was the construction and furnishing of a four-classroom block by Akinmade, who also provided a generator to address the school’s power needs. Similarly, Dr. Munirat Ogunlayi undertook the renovation of the school hall, while Mr. Oluwole Adelabu renovated the staff office and administrative block to improve the working environment for teachers and other personnel. The alumni also facilitated the construction of a perimeter fence to strengthen security within the school premises and protect its facilities, alongside the donation of exercise books to support students. In a further demonstration of their commitment to students’ welfare, the old students established a Student Support Programme to assist indigent students with the financial requirements for their Junior Secondary School examinations and West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE). Akinmade said the projects were conceived to address critical infrastructure needs, expand available classroom space and improve the general condition of the institution. He called on other former students to identify with the school and contribute to its continued development, stressing that the future of public education required collective responsibility and sustained commitment. The celebration brought together alumni, teachers, students and other stakeholders to reflect on the institution’s 50-year history, celebrate its achievements and renew their commitment to its growth. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/a.title_zh: 阿耶达蒂瓦敦促校友和利益相关方扭转公立学校基础设施短缺局面
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/a.body_zh: Ondo State 州长 Lucky Aiyedatiwa 呼吁全国公立学校中经济条件较好的校友投资母校的发展，并表示，提供优质教育和充足基础设施的责任不应完全由政府承担。州长在 Akure 的 Omo’luorogbo Grammar School 庆祝建校50周年之际发出倡议，呼吁昔日学生和其他利益相关方通过弥补基础设施缺口、改善公立学校的学习环境，补充政府的努力。由物理规划与城市发展事务委员 Sunday Olajide 先生代表出席的 Lucky Aiyedatiwa 表示，校友作出的实质性贡献，对于维持教育机构的运转以及确保年轻一代能够使用优质学习设施，仍然至关重要。他指出，政府无法独自承担教育领域庞大的资金需求，并强调，与昔日学生、企业和其他利益相关方建立合作关系，将加快公立学校的发展。据他介绍，这次金禧庆典为校友提供了机会，以表达对学校的感激之情；正是这所学校为他们的个人和职业成就奠定了基础。他说：“政府无法独自完成这件事。我们需要昔日学生和其他利益相关方的支持，补充我们在公立学校提供优质教育和改善基础设施方面的努力。”州长补充说，对教育进行集体投资，将有助于弥补现有的基础设施缺口，营造更有利于教学和学习的环境。50周年庆典筹备委员会主席、前 Ondo State 新闻事务委员 Kayode Akinmade 先生在活动上表示，校友决定以实际项目纪念学校的金禧庆典，改善学校设施并支持在校生的学业发展。Akinmade 将回馈学校视为一种责任，而不是慈善行为，并指出，这所学校为许多昔日学生打造成功职业生涯奠定了基础。他说，这些介入措施旨在确保现在和未来的学生拥有更好的学习条件，并补充道，校友决心通过可持续投资传承学校的优良传统。已实施的项目包括由 Akinmade 出资建设并配置设施的一栋四层教室楼，他还提供了一台发电机，以满足学校的用电需求。同样，Munirat Ogunlayi 博士负责翻修了学校礼堂，Oluwole Adelabu 先生则翻新了教职员工办公室和行政楼，以改善教师及其他工作人员的工作环境。校友还推动修建了校园周边围栏，以加强校园内部安全并保护学校设施，同时捐赠练习本，为学生提供支持。为进一步体现对学生的关怀，昔日学生设立了 Student Support Programme，帮助经济困难的学生支付 Junior Secondary School 考试和 West African Senior School Certificate Examination（WASSCE）所需的费用。Akinmade 表示，这些项目旨在满足关键基础设施需求、扩大可用教室空间并改善学校的整体状况。他呼吁其他昔日学生认同母校并为学校的持续发展作出贡献，强调公共教育的未来需要集体责任和持续承诺。此次庆典汇聚了校友、教师、学生和其他利益相关方，共同回顾学校50年的历史，庆祝其成就，并重申推动学校发展的承诺。THISDAY 创办于1995年1月22日，由 THISDAY NEWSPAPARS LTD. 出版，地址为35 Creek Road Apapa, Lagos, Nigeria，并在 Nigeria 的36个州、Federal Capital Territory 以及世界各地设有办公室。它是 Nigeria 面向政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛中产阶级的最具权威性新闻媒体，覆盖所有平台，同时作为有志人士和千禧一代汇聚新思想、文化与技术的交汇点。这份报纸秉持公共信托精神，致力于追求真理与理性，报道从突发新闻到政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育和社区等广泛议题，触及人与社会的交汇点。您可以发送邮件至 hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的“联系我们”页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/3.title: 388 States, FCT Officials Undergo Capacity-building Training on Effective Budget Planning
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/3.summary: The training supported states to prioritise cost, map and geo-tagging of projects and reconcile their sector Workplans with available budget ceilings. the four-batch capacity-building workshop, will conclude on November 4, 2026.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/3.summary_zh: 此次培训支持各州优先确定项目的成本，进行项目制图和地理标记，并使各部门的工作计划与可用的预算上限保持一致。这场分四批举行的能力建设研讨会将于2026年11月4日结束。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/3.body: The HOPE Governance Programme is a $500 million World Bank-supported programme designed to address critical governance, financing, transparency and accountability constraints affecting the delivery of basic education and primary healthcare services. The workshop was also designed to enhance the practical application of the National Chart of Accounts and programme-based budgetting in the basic education and primary health care sectors. The training supported states to prioritise cost, map and geo-tagging of projects and reconcile their sector Workplans with available budget ceilings. It also identified and addressed state-specific planning and budgeting gaps through practical, hands-on exercises using actual state documents. the four-batch capacity-building workshop, will conclude on November 4, 2026. He said the National Coordinator, Dr. Assad Hassan disclosed in Abuja on Monday that the event was timed to match ongoing 2027 states’ budget preparations. According to Hassan, the strategic timing was to ensure that states budgets properly align with the National Chart of Accounts based on the Programme’s Disbursement-Linked Indicator 2 (DLI 2). “This workshop is designed to strengthen the capacity of State institutions to align their Annual Operational Plans for Primary Healthcare and Annual Consolidated Workplans for Basic Education with their respective budgets. “Achieving the objectives of DLI 2 requires a coordinated, multisectoral approach. This is why the composition of participants in this room is deliberate, bringing together key institutions and stakeholders from the budget, primary healthcare and basic education sectors. Effective collaboration among these institutions is essential to ensuring that planning, budgeting and implementation are properly aligned,” he said. According to Hassan, budget should reflect what government intends to achieve, not simply what government intends to spend, hence planning must drive budgeting, and budgeting must ultimately support service delivery. “A good plan without a budget is an aspiration; a budget without a plan is an invitation to inefficiency,” he stated. In her remarks on the occasion, the Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning, Dr. Deborah Odoh, said the participation of senior states officials in the workshop was to ensure that the technical work undertaken translates into institutional decisions that will improve budgeting and implementation in the states. She pledged the commitment of the ministry through the HOPE Governance Programme, to work with state governments and the World Bank with a view to strengthening public financial management systems and boosting the delivery of essential services to the citizens. Speaking at the event, the World Bank Task Team Lead for the HOPE Governance Programme, Mr. Ikechukwu Nweje disclosed that states stand to receive significant incentives upon achieving DLI 2. He reaffirmed the World Bank’s commitment to supporting state governments in implementing critical governance reforms aimed at improving service delivery in basic education and primary healthcare.
