https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/3.title_zh: 388名州及联邦首都领地官员接受有效预算规划能力建设培训
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/3.body_zh: HOPE治理方案是一项由世界银行支持的5亿美元计划，旨在解决影响基础教育和初级医疗服务提供的关键治理、融资、透明度及问责限制。此次研讨会还旨在加强国家会计科目表以及基础教育和初级医疗部门项目预算编制的实际应用。培训支持各州确定项目优先事项、绘制项目地图并进行地理标注，同时将各部门的业务工作计划与可用预算上限进行核对。培训还通过使用各州实际文件开展实践练习，识别并处理各州特有的规划和预算缺口。这场分四批举行的能力建设研讨会将于2026年11月4日结束。他表示，国家协调员Assad Hassan博士周一在阿布贾透露，此次活动的时间安排与各州正在进行的2027年预算编制工作相衔接。Hassan称，选择这一时间节点是为了确保各州预算能够根据该方案的拨款挂钩指标2（DLI 2）与国家会计科目表正确衔接。他说：“本次研讨会旨在加强各州机构的能力，使其能够将初级医疗年度业务计划和基础教育年度综合工作计划与各自预算相对应。“实现DLI 2的目标需要协调一致、跨部门的方法。这正是本次研讨会参与者的构成经过周密安排的原因，来自预算、初级医疗和基础教育部门的重要机构及利益相关方齐聚一堂。这些机构之间的有效合作，对于确保规划、预算编制和执行工作正确协调至关重要。”他说。Hassan表示，预算应当反映政府打算实现的目标，而不只是政府打算花费的资金，因此规划必须推动预算编制，而预算编制最终必须支持服务交付。他指出：“没有预算的良好规划只是愿望；没有规划的预算则是对低效率的邀请。”联邦预算和经济规划部常任秘书Deborah Odoh博士在此次活动中致辞时表示，各州高级官员参加研讨会，是为了确保所开展的技术工作转化为制度层面的决定，从而改善各州的预算编制和执行工作。她承诺，该部将通过HOPE治理方案与各州政府及世界银行合作，以加强公共财政管理体系，并提升面向公民的基本服务交付。HOPE治理方案世界银行任务组组长Ikechukwu Nweje先生在活动上表示，各州在实现DLI 2后可获得丰厚激励。他重申，世界银行承诺支持各州政府实施关键治理改革，以改善基础教育和初级医疗服务的交付。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创办，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕溪路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都区以及世界各地设有办事处。该报是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，覆盖所有平台，服务于政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级，同时为有志者和千禧一代提供新思想、文化和技术的交汇点。该报秉持公共信托精神致力于追求真相和理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育和社区等议题，直至人与社会的交汇点。您可以发送邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/l.title: LIFE-ND Trains 200 Agribusiness Beneficiaries in Fourth Batch in Imo
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/l.summary: The Imo State Livelihood Improvement Family Enterprises – Niger Delta (LIFE-ND) Project has trained 200 new agribusiness beneficiaries in its fourth batch in the state as part of efforts to promote entrepreneurship, enhance food security and create sustainable livelihood opportunities for youths and women.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/l.summary_zh: 伊莫州生计改善家庭企业——尼日尔河三角洲（LIFE-ND）项目已在该州完成第四批200名新型农业企业受益者的培训，旨在促进创业、增强粮食安全，并为青年和女性创造可持续的生计机会。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/l.body: The Imo State Livelihood Improvement Family Enterprises – Niger Delta (LIFE-ND) Project has trained 200 new agribusiness beneficiaries in its fourth batch in the state as part of efforts to promote entrepreneurship, enhance food security and create sustainable livelihood opportunities for youths and women. The training commenced with an orientation programme held at Newton Hotel, Owerri, on Friday, October 30, 2026. Addressing participants at the ceremony, the Imo State Project Coordinator, Chief (Mrs.) Victoria Igboanugo, described the programme as the beginning of an important journey towards acquiring practical agribusiness skills, promoting entrepreneurship and building sustainable livelihoods. She explained the orientation was designed to expose participants to critical aspects of agribusiness development, including climate change awareness, nutrition mainstreaming, record-keeping, gender inclusion and the application of technology in agricultural production and enterprise management. Igboanugo disclosed the project had previously trained and empowered 1,403 beneficiaries across its first three batches. She further revealed the 200 beneficiaries selected for the fourth batch emerged from a pool of 1,021 applicants through an electronic selection process, describing the exercise as a transparent approach to identifying qualified participants. The Project Coordinator charged the incubators to provide effective mentorship, practical guidance and the necessary support to ensure that the trainees acquired the requisite skills to establish and manage successful agribusiness enterprises. She also urged the incubatees to demonstrate discipline, commitment and a strong willingness to learn, stressing that their dedication would determine their success as future agripreneurs. “Your dedication throughout this programme will play a significant role in determining your success as future agripreneurs,” she said. She expressed appreciation to the National Project Coordinator and his team, the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), and the Imo State Government, under the leadership of Governor Hope Uzodimma, for their continued support and commitment to the successful implementation of the LIFE-ND Project. In a goodwill message on behalf of the NDDC Managing Director, Dr. Samuel Ogbuku, the Commission noted that its funding of the project in Imo, Rivers and Akwa Ibom States represented a deliberate investment in the future of the people of the Niger Delta. “We believe that true development begins with empowering our youths with viable skills in agriculture – a sector with immense potential for income generation, food security and job creation,” the statement read. Also speaking, the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture, Dr. Alexander Onwumere, who represented the Commissioner for Agriculture and Food Security, commended Igboanugo for her commitment to the success of the project and encouraged her to sustain the momentum. In an interview, one of the beneficiaries, Mrs. Chioma Nwosu, expressed gratitude to the Federal Government for the opportunity to participate in the programme. “Indeed, I am happy today to have participated in this programme. My heart is filled with joy,” she said. The ceremony was attended by the representative of the Imo State Governor; the Commissioner for Agriculture and Food Security; the Honourable Commissioner representing Imo State on the NDDC Board; the National Project Coordinator of LIFE-ND; officials of the project; incubators; incubatees; and other stakeholders. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/l.title_zh: LIFE-ND在Imo州为第四批200名农业企业受益人提供培训
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/l.body_zh: 伊莫州生计改善家庭企业—尼日尔河三角洲（LIFE-ND）项目已在该州为第四批200名新的农业综合企业受益人开展培训，旨在促进创业、提高粮食保障能力，并为青年和女性创造可持续的生计机会。培训于2026年10月30日星期五在奥韦里牛顿酒店举行的入门培训活动拉开帷幕。伊莫州项目协调员维多利亚·伊博阿努戈女士酋长在仪式上向参与者致辞，称该培训开启了一段重要旅程，参与者将由此掌握实用的农业综合企业技能、促进创业并建立可持续的生计。她表示，此次入门培训旨在让参与者了解农业综合企业发展的关键环节，包括气候变化意识、营养主流化、记录管理、性别包容，以及技术在农业生产和企业管理中的应用。伊博阿努戈透露，该项目此前已通过前三批培训赋能1,403名受益人。她进一步表示，入选第四批的200名受益人是从1,021名申请者中经过电子遴选程序产生的，并将这一遴选称为识别合格参与者的透明方式。项目协调员要求各孵化机构提供有效辅导、实践指导和必要支持，确保受训者获得建立和经营成功农业综合企业所需的技能。她还敦促受孵化企业人员表现出纪律、投入精神以及强烈的学习意愿，强调他们的投入程度将决定其未来成为农业企业家的成败。她说：“在整个项目期间，你们的投入将在决定你们未来能否成为农业企业家方面发挥重要作用。”她向国家项目协调员及其团队、尼日尔河三角洲发展委员会（NDDC），以及在州长霍普·乌佐迪马领导下的伊莫州政府表示感谢，感谢各方持续支持并致力于推动LIFE-ND项目成功实施。委员会在尼日尔河三角洲发展委员会常务董事萨缪尔·奥格布库博士的授权下发布友好致辞，对该项目表示赞赏，称其为该委员会在伊莫州、 Rivers州和阿夸伊博姆州提供资金，是一项旨在投资尼日尔河三角洲人民未来的明确举措。声明称：“我们相信，真正的发展始于赋予青年实用的农业技能——农业在创造收入、保障粮食安全和促进就业方面拥有巨大潜力。”农业部常任秘书亚历山大·奥努梅雷博士也出席活动并发言。他代表农业与粮食安全事务专员，对伊博阿努戈致力于推动项目成功表示赞赏，并鼓励她延续当前势头。一名受益人奇奥马·恩沃苏夫人在接受采访时，对联邦政府给予参与该项目的机会表示感谢。她说：“今天能够参与这个项目，我确实感到高兴，内心充满了喜悦。”伊莫州州长代表、农业与粮食安全事务专员、代表伊莫州出任尼日尔河三角洲发展委员会董事会成员的尊敬的专员、LIFE-ND国家项目协调员、项目官员、孵化机构、受孵化企业人员及其他利益相关方出席了仪式。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创办，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕溪路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区以及世界各地设有办公室。对于政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级而言，它是尼日利亚可在所有平台上获取的最具权威性的新闻媒体，同时充当抱负人士和千禧一代探索新思想、文化与技术的交汇点。该报秉持公共信托精神，致力于追求真相与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育和社区，以及人与社会的交汇议题。您可以发送邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/j.title: Jibrin, Abbas Push Stronger Regulation to Transform Nigeria’s Real Estate Sector
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/j.summary: Abdulmumini Jibrin, has advocated stronger legislation and a comprehensive regulatory framework to tackle the numerous challenges hindering the growth of Nigeria’s housing and real estate sector.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/j.summary_zh: 阿卜杜勒穆米尼·吉布林主张加强立法并建立全面的监管框架，以应对阻碍尼日利亚住房和房地产行业发展的众多挑战。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/j.body: • As minister assures of more government efforts to tackle sectoral challenges Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Housing and Habitat, Hon. Abdulmumini Jibrin, has advocated stronger legislation and a comprehensive regulatory framework to tackle the numerous challenges hindering the growth of Nigeria’s housing and real estate sector. Jibrin said the introduction of an effective regulatory structure would help maximise the vast opportunities in the housing industry, enhance transparency and accountability, encourage investments, safeguard homebuyers and ultimately expand access to affordable housing for Nigerians. The lawmaker disclosed that since assuming leadership of the House Committee on Housing and Habitat, he had conducted a comprehensive review of the sector to identify its challenges, explore available opportunities and assess its potential contributions to Nigeria’s economic growth. He explained the assessment showed the country is yet to take advantage of even a small portion of the opportunities in the housing industry, largely because of regulatory deficiencies, overlapping mandates among government institutions, weak consumer protection mechanisms and the absence of a unified national framework. According to him, although the Minister of Housing and Urban Development is saddled with the responsibility of implementing government policies in the sector, several agencies and institutions whose activities are connected to housing operate outside the ministry’s direct control, resulting in institutional gaps and duplication of responsibilities. “There are enormous challenges. We have a wonderful Minister of Housing. But as the Minister of Housing of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, he does not have jurisdiction over all the agencies and institutions that have to do with housing. There is a link; there is a gap. So, there is duplication of functions,” he said. He noted that some individuals enter into housing arrangements without properly considering their financial capacity, while others fail to understand prevailing economic conditions, changes in government policies and inflationary pressures that could affect developers’ ability to complete projects based on their initial agreements. The Committee Chairman stressed that a well-regulated housing industry must clearly define the obligations of developers and consumers, establish efficient dispute resolution mechanisms and ensure that all participants comply with clearly established operational standards. He described the housing industry as a significant contributor to Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP), adding that its contribution to the national economy could increase considerably if the opportunities within the sector were properly explored and utilised. Jibrin further observed that unlike other critical sectors of the economy, such as oil and gas, electricity and telecommunications, the real estate industry had continued to operate with considerable regulatory loopholes, making it possible for individuals to engage in property development without sufficient scrutiny, supervision or accountability. He explained that unscrupulous individuals could easily circulate property brochures to unsuspecting Nigerians and collect payments without any effective institutional mechanism to authenticate their credentials, assess their business operations or establish their capacity to execute the proposed projects. According to him, the proposed legislation is intended to bridge this regulatory gap by creating a national framework that would reinforce existing institutions without interfering with their legally assigned responsibilities. He also dismissed concerns that the proposed National Real Estate Regulatory Authority would undermine the constitutional powers of state governments or assume the statutory duties of established professional associations and regulatory bodies. “The bill to create the National Housing Regulatory Authority is not going to take over the powers of any state government. We are not going to compete. We are only going to cooperate. And for professional bodies, nobody is taking away your responsibility. It will be protected. “For government agencies, it will strengthen you and ensure that every government agency is empowered to perform its statutory role according to its Act,” he stated. He added that the proposed authority should be regarded as more than the establishment of another regulatory agency, describing it as a strategic measure to maximise the economic opportunities in the housing industry by resolving longstanding institutional weaknesses and regulatory shortcomings. Speaking at the event, the Minister of Housing and Urban Development, Dr. Muttaqha Rabe Darma, said the federal government was stepping up efforts to resolve the structural and institutional problems affecting the country’s housing sector. The minister revealed that the Ministry had convened a similar stakeholders’ meeting in July, where challenges relating to Nigeria’s housing deficit were examined and validated, with available estimates putting the shortfall at more than 15 million housing units. He observed that despite Nigeria’s estimated population of approximately 240 million, mortgage financing remained largely inaccessible, compared with the situation in several other countries, thereby limiting the ability of many citizens to own decent and affordable homes. “Our population, as of today, is estimated to be about 240 million, but as speakers after speakers mentioned, mortgage penetration is very low. It is less than 10 per cent, as against 38 per cent in Malaysia and 40 per cent in South Korea,” he said. Darma noted that although the country had institutions such as the Federal Mortgage Bank and other mortgage financing organisations, the number of mortgage facilities provided annually remained insufficient to address the nation’s housing requirements. He also recalled that the built environment and real estate industry had been ranked as the third-largest contributor to Nigeria’s economy, emphasising the importance of creating favourable conditions that would enable the sector to operate more efficiently and maximise its contributions. The minister expressed the Federal Ministry of Housing and Urban Development’s support for the conference and the proposed establishment of the regulatory authority, noting that the initiative could strengthen coordination in housing delivery, real estate investments and mortgage financing. However, he urged stakeholders to examine the possibility of placing the proposed authority under the supervision of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Development to promote effective coordination and ensure consistency with the federal government’s existing housing policies. He explained that countries such as Singapore, Dubai, Malaysia, the United Kingdom and Rwanda had adopted similar arrangements with comparable regulatory institutions operating within ministries responsible for housing and the built environment. Darma also called for a coordinated working relationship among the proposed authority, the National Housing Finance Authority and the mortgage policy being developed by the federal government, which is currently awaiting presidential consideration. In his remarks, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Ministry of Finance Incorporated (MOFI), Dr. Armstrong Ume Takang, applauded the House of Representatives for maintaining its collaboration with the Executive arm of government in addressing the challenges facing the housing and real estate industry. Takang assured that the presidency and the federal government were prepared to give the proposed legislation adequate and objective consideration, particularly regarding critical concerns surrounding the country’s existing legal and institutional arrangements. He identified the relationship between the proposed law and the Land Use Act as one of the major areas requiring careful attention, alongside the regulation of professional practices and the need to avoid excessive regulatory requirements that could discourage private sector participation and investment. The MOFI chief executive further urged stakeholders to design a regulatory framework that would strengthen and complement existing government institutions without creating unnecessary bureaucratic structures or increasing the government’s recurrent expenditure. “To what extent are we going to address the regulation of practice in this sector? To what extent are we also going to ensure that the sector is not overregulated? And how do we create this new agency and fit it into the existing structure of government in a way that we do not expand the recurrent expenditure framework of government?” he queried. He assured participants of the government’s willingness to work with relevant stakeholders towards building a more robust, transparent and sustainable housing and real estate industry that would attract investments and deliver greater economic benefits to the country. Also delivering the keynote address, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Abbas Tajudeen, advocated the creation of a centralised and digitalised real estate administrative system to simplify property transactions, boost public confidence and position Nigeria’s housing market as an attractive destination for domestic and international investors. Abbas stressed the importance of establishing a dependable digital connection between property ownership records and the identities of their owners, as well as between buyers and sellers, to curb fraud, resolve cases of multiple ownership claims and minimise disputes arising from land and property transactions. In his keynote address titled, “Building a Trusted and Investable Nigerian Real Estate Market,” the Speaker maintained that Nigeria’s housing problem was not necessarily caused by a lack of available properties but by inadequate trust and confidence in the country’s real estate market. “Nigeria does not lack property. Nigeria lacks enough trust in property,” he said. He argued that proper regulation should not be seen as a barrier to genuine business activities but as an essential mechanism for protecting the industry against fraudulent dealings, unhealthy competition and the exploitation of unsuspecting investors and prospective homeowners. According to the Speaker, effective regulation provides protection for credible businesses, strengthens market confidence and establishes the institutional credibility needed to attract sustainable, long-term investments into the housing sector. The proposed National Real Estate Regulatory Authority is expected to establish a coordinated regulatory structure for Nigeria’s housing and real estate industry, improve consumer protection, enforce professional standards and address institutional shortcomings that have continued to impede the sector’s growth and development. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/j.title_zh: Jibrin和Abbas推动加强监管，以改造尼日利亚房地产行业
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/j.body_zh: 众议院住房与居住环境委员会主席阿卜杜勒穆米尼·吉布林表示，部长承诺政府将采取更多措施应对行业挑战；吉布林主张制定更有力的立法和全面的监管框架，以解决阻碍尼日利亚住房和房地产行业发展的诸多难题。吉布林说，建立有效的监管结构有助于充分挖掘住房行业的巨大机遇，提高透明度和问责制，鼓励投资，保护购房者，并最终扩大尼日利亚民众获得可负担住房的机会。这位议员透露，自担任众议院住房与居住环境委员会主席以来，他对该行业进行了全面审查，以识别其面临的挑战、探索现有机遇并评估该行业对尼日利亚经济增长的潜在贡献。他解释说，评估结果显示 owing to 监管不足、政府机构职责重叠、消费者保护机制薄弱以及缺乏统一的全国框架，尼日利亚尚未利用住房行业哪怕一小部分的机遇。据他介绍，尽管住房与城市发展部长肩负着落实政府在该领域政策的职责，但多个与住房有关的机构和组织并不受该部直接控制，导致机构职能之间出现缺口和重复。“挑战非常巨大。我们有一位非常优秀的住房部长。但作为尼日利亚联邦共和国住房部长，他并不管辖所有与住房有关的机构和组织。这些机构之间存在联系，也存在缺口。因此，职能出现了重复。”他说。他指出，有些人在没有充分考虑自身经济能力的情况下便签订住房安排，另一些人则未能了解可能影响开发商按照最初协议完成项目能力的经济形势、政府政策变化和通胀压力。委员会主席强调，受良好监管的住房行业必须明确界定开发商和消费者的义务，建立高效的争端解决机制，并确保所有参与者遵守明确制定的操作标准。他称，住房行业是尼日利亚国内生产总值（GDP）的重要贡献者；如果该行业的机遇得到适当探索和利用，其对国民经济的贡献可大幅增加。吉布林进一步指出，与石油天然气、电力和电信等其他关键经济行业相比，房地产行业一直存在大量监管漏洞，使个人可以在缺乏充分审查、监督或问责的情况下从事房地产开发。他解释说，不法分子很容易向毫无戒心的尼日利亚民众散发房产宣传册并收取款项，却没有任何有效的机构机制核实其资质、评估其经营情况或确认其履行拟建项目的能力。据他称，拟议立法旨在通过建立全国框架弥合这一监管缺口，在不干预现有机构依法履行职责的情况下强化这些机构。他还驳斥了有关拟议中的全国房地产监管局会削弱州政府宪法权力或取代现有专业协会与监管机构法定职责的担忧。他说：“设立全国住房监管局的法案不会接管任何州政府的权力。我们不会与其竞争，只会与其合作。对于专业机构，不会有人剥夺你们的责任，这些责任将受到保护。对于政府机构，该局将强化其职能，确保每个政府机构都能依据相关法案获得授权，履行法定职责。”他补充说，拟议监管局不应被视为仅仅再设立一个监管机构，而应被视为通过解决长期存在的机构薄弱环节和监管缺陷，最大程度释放住房行业经济机遇的战略措施。住房与城市发展部长穆塔卡·拉贝·达尔马博士在活动上表示，联邦政府正在加大努力，解决影响该国住房行业的结构性和机构性问题。部长透露，该部曾于7月召集类似的利益相关方会议，对与尼日利亚住房短缺有关的挑战进行审查和核实，现有估计显示缺口超过1500万套住房。他指出，尽管尼日利亚人口估计约为2.4亿，但与若干其他国家相比，按揭融资仍大多难以获得，从而限制了許多公民拥有体面且可负担住房的能力。“截至目前，我们的人口估计约为2.4亿，但正如一位又一位发言者所指出的，按揭渗透率非常低，低于10%，而马来西亚为38%，韩国为40%。”他说。达尔马指出，尽管该国拥有联邦抵押贷款银行及其他按揭融资组织，但每年提供的按揭额度仍不足以满足全国住房需求。他还提到，建筑环境和房地产行业已 ranked 为对尼日利亚经济贡献第三大的行业，并强调有必要创造有利条件，使该行业能够更高效运作并最大限度扩大贡献。部长表示，联邦住房与城市发展部支持本次会议及设立监管局的提议，并指出该举措可以加强住房交付、房地产投资和按揭融资之间的协调。不过，他敦促利益相关方研究将拟议监管局置于住房与城市发展部监督之下的可能性，以促进有效协调，并确保其与联邦政府现有住房政策保持一致。他解释说，新加坡、迪拜、马来西亚、英国和卢旺达等已采取类似安排，由各住房与建筑环境主管部门内部的同类监管机构开展监管。达尔马还呼吁拟议监管局、全国住房融资管理局与联邦政府正在制定且目前尚待总统审议的按揭政策之间建立协调协作关系。财政部公司（MOFI）董事兼首席执行官阿姆斯特朗·乌梅·塔坎博士在发言中赞扬众议院继续与政府行政机构合作，处理住房和房地产行业面临的挑战。塔坎保证，总统府和联邦政府准备对拟议立法进行充分而客观的审议，尤其重视围绕该国现有法律和机构安排的关键问题。他指出，拟议法律与《土地使用法》之间的关系是需要谨慎处理的主要领域之一，同时还包括专业实务监管，以及避免设置过度监管要求而抑制私营部门参与和投资。MOFI首席执行官进一步敦促利益相关方设计一套能够强化并补充现有政府机构的监管框架，同时避免造成不必要的官僚结构或增加政府经常性支出。他质问道：“我们将多大程度处理该行业的执业监管？我们又将多大程度确保该行业不受过度监管？以及，我们如何设立这个新机构，并将其纳入现有政府架构，同时不扩大政府的经常性支出框架？”他向与会者保证，政府愿意与相关利益相关方合作，建设更稳健、透明和可持续的住房与房地产行业，吸引投资并为该国带来更大的经济利益。众议院议长阿巴斯·塔朱丁爵士发表主旨演讲，倡议建立集中化、数字化的房地产行政系统，以简化房产交易、提振公众信心，并将尼日利亚住房市场打造为对国内外投资者具有吸引力的目的地。阿巴斯强调，需要在房产所有权记录与业主身份之间，以及买卖双方之间建立可靠的数字连接，以遏制欺诈、解决多重产权主张案件，并尽量减少土地和房产交易引发的争端。在题为《建设值得信赖且具有投资吸引力的尼日利亚房地产市场》的主旨演讲中，议长坚持认为，尼日利亚的住房问题未必源于可获得房产不足，而在于对该国房地产市场缺乏足够的信任和信心。他说：“尼日利亚不缺房产，缺的是人们对房产的足够信任。”他认为，恰当监管不应被视为正当商业活动的障碍，而应视为保护行业免受欺诈交易、不良竞争以及剥削毫无戒心的投资者和准业主的必要机制。议长表示，有效监管能够保护信誉良好的企业、增强市场信心，并建立吸引住房行业可持续长期投资所需的机构公信力。拟议中的全国房地产监管局预计将建立协调统一的监管结构，改善消费者保护，执行行业标准，并解决持续阻碍该行业增长和发展的机构缺陷。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创办，由THISDAY https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/31/t.body: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has approved the appointment of Professor Murtala Muhammad Ahmad as the seventh substantive Chief Medical Director (CMD) of the Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital (UDUTH), Sokoto. In a statement by the Head, Public Affairs, UDUTH, Mansur Wadata, the appointment is for an initial term of four years with effect from October 20, 2026, and was conveyed in a letter signed by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate. Professor Ahmad succeeds Professor Anas Ahmad Sabir, who successfully completed his two-term tenure in May this year. The statement further stated that while congratulating him on the appointment, Professor Pate reminded him of the heavy responsibilities of his new office and the yearnings of Nigerians for an effective and responsive healthcare delivery system. He urged the new CMD to justify the confidence reposed in him by Mr. President by working collaboratively with all stakeholders to ensure that the hospital continues to deliver quality healthcare services to Nigerians. Professor Ahmad becomes the second alumnus of the Usmanu Danfodiyo University to lead the Teaching Hospital as Chief Medical Director, marking a historic milestone for the institution. With over two decades of experience in Paediatrics and Child Health, Professor Ahmad brings a robust blend of clinical expertise, university teaching, and hospital administration to his new role. He earned his Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) degree from the Usmanu Danfodiyo University, followed by a Fellowship of the West African College of Physicians (FWACP) in Paediatrics and a Professional Diploma in Education from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria. He also holds specialized certifications in paediatric electroencephalography, health leadership, management, and public administration from the University of Cape Town, University of Washington and Administrative Staff College of Nigeria (ASCON) respectively. Before his elevation, Professor Ahmad built an impressive administrative track record within both the university and the teaching hospital, steadily climbing the academic ladder from Lecturer I to Senior Lecturer, Reader, and ultimately Professor of Paediatrics. He previously served as Deputy Chairman of the Medical Advisory Committee (Training) at UDUTH for four years, where he brought impactful transformation to the administration of residency and training in the hospital. He also held key roles as Deputy Director of the Institute of Child Health and Faculty Examinations Officer in the Faculty of Clinical Sciences, alongside representing the faculty on the University Senate, and stepped in as Acting Chairman of the Medical Advisory Committee and Acting Chief Medical Director on multiple occasions. Beyond institutional management, Professor Ahmad has been at the forefront of public health service and specialised medical research in Sokoto State and across Nigeria, with active involvement in maternal and perinatal death surveillance and response, and as a national trainer on the management of severe acute malnutrition. As a prolific researcher, he has published widely in peer-reviewed journals focusing on child health, child neurology, epilepsy, and broader paediatric health concerns, while actively mentoring the next generation of medical professionals and postgraduate students. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/31/t.title_zh: Tinubu任命Ahmad教授为UDUTH首席医疗官
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/31/t.body_zh: 总统Bola Ahmed Tinubu已批准任命Murtala Muhammad Ahmad教授为位于Sokoto的Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital（UDUTH）第七任正式首席医务主任（CMD）。UDUTH公共事务负责人Mansur Wadata在一份声明中表示，此次任命的首个任期为4年，自2026年10月20日起生效，任命通知由卫生与社会保障协调部长Muhammad Ali Pate教授签署的函件传达。Pate教授在声明中进一步表示，他祝贺Ahmad教授获得任命，同时提醒他将承担新职位赋予的重任，以及尼日利亚人民对高效且能及时回应的医疗服务体系的期待。他敦促新任CMD通过与所有利益相关方协作，不辜负总统先生对他的信任，确保医院继续为尼日利亚人民提供优质医疗服务。Ahmad教授成为第二位以首席医务主任身份领导该教学医院的Usmanu Danfodiyo University校友，标志该校迎来历史性里程碑。Ahmad教授拥有20多年的儿科和儿童健康经验，将丰富的临床专业能力、大学教学经验和医院管理经验融入新职位。他从Usmanu Danfodiyo University取得医学学士与外科学士（MBBS）学位，随后取得西非内科医师学院（FWACP）儿科专业进修资格，并从Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria取得教育专业文凭。他还从University of Cape Town取得儿科脑电图和健康领导力认证，从University of Washington取得管理认证，并从Administrative Staff College of Nigeria（ASCON）取得公共行政认证。在此次晋升之前，Ahmad教授在大学和教学医院都取得了出色的行政管理成绩，并逐步晋升学术职级，先后担任一级讲师、高级讲师、Reader，最终成为儿科教授。他此前在UDUTH担任医学咨询委员会（培训）副主席4年，期间推动医院住院医师培训及培训管理工作的 impactful 转型。他还曾担任儿童健康研究所副所长、临床科学学院考试事务官等重要职务，代表学院参加大学评议会，并多次代理医学咨询委员会主席和首席医务主任职务。除机构管理外，Ahmad教授还一直处于Sokoto州及尼日利亚各地公共卫生服务和专业医疗研究的前沿，积极参与孕产妇和围产期死亡监测与应对工作，并担任重度急性营养不良管理领域的全国培训师。作为成果丰硕的研究者，他在同行评审期刊上广泛发表研究论文，重点关注儿童健康、儿童神经病学、癫痫以及更广泛的儿科健康问题，同时积极指导下一代医疗专业人员和研究生。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创办，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为35 Creek Road Apapa, Lagos, Nigeria，并在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区及世界各地设有办公室。该报是面向政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛中产阶层的尼日利亚最具权威性的全平台新闻媒体，同时为有抱负者和千禧一代提供汇聚新思想、文化与技术的交汇点。该报秉持公共信托精神，致力于追求真相与理性，报道范围从突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育和社区延伸至人与社会的交汇点。您可以发送电子邮件至hello@thisdaylive.com或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/b.summary: The proposal, which also provides for three additional seats for women in each of the 36 state Houses of Assembly, is designed to expand women’s participation in legislative decision-making without displacing existing constituencies or elected lawmakers. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/b.summary_zh: 该提案还规定，在36个州议会中各增加3个女性席位，旨在扩大女性参与立法决策的范围，同时不取代现有选区或当选议员。兼任参议院1999年宪法审查委员会副主席的Bamidele表示，该提案是第10届全国议会正在进行的宪法修订工作的一部分。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/b.body: • Says proposal allocates 37 seats each to Senate, House of Representatives •Three additional seats proposed for women in each state assembly The National Assembly has proposed the creation of 74 additional seats exclusively reserved for women in Senate and House of Representatives as part of ongoing efforts to address gender imbalance in Nigeria’s political representation. The proposal, which also provides for three additional seats for women in each of the 36 state Houses of Assembly, is designed to expand women’s participation in legislative decision-making without displacing existing constituencies or elected lawmakers. Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, disclosed the proposal on Monday while speaking at the 2026 Law Week organised by the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA), Ekiti State Chapter. Bamidele, who is also Vice Chairman of Senate Committee on the Review of the 1999 Constitution, said the proposal formed part of the ongoing constitution amendment exercise being undertaken by the 10th National Assembly. He explained that the proposed arrangement would provide 37 additional seats in Senate and another 37 in House of Representatives, ensuring that every state of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory would have one additional representative in each chamber. According to him, the proposed special seats are intended to provide women with greater access to elective positions and decision-making platforms, particularly against the background of their historically low representation in Nigeria’s legislative institutions. Bamidele disclosed that the Constitution Review Committee had also recommended three additional seats for women in each State House of Assembly. He stressed that the proposed seats would be exclusively reserved for women and would not affect existing electoral constituencies or displace any serving lawmaker. The arrangement, he added, would operate for 16 years, covering four electoral cycles, after which it would undergo a comprehensive review. Bamidele explained, “This arrangement is proposed to run for a period of 16 years, four electoral cycles, before a comprehensive review. This is a sunset clause designed to ensure sustainability and to allow for the organic development of a more inclusive political culture.” The senate leader expressed confidence that the proposal would secure the necessary legislative backing, particularly from the state Houses of Assembly, whose approval is constitutionally required to complete the amendment process. “We are actively and strategically engaging with the State Houses of Assembly, as their concurrence is a constitutional sine qua non for bringing this reform to fruition,” he said. Bamidele described the proposed special seats as a fundamental democratic reform rather than a partisan political initiative, stating that a representative democracy cannot function effectively while excluding a substantial proportion of the population from legislative decision-making. He said the initiative followed extensive consultations and consensus-building, adding that the National Assembly deliberately commenced the constitutional review process early to allow sufficient time for scrutiny and wider stakeholder participation. He said the 10th National Assembly’s commitment to the initiative had also been strengthened by advocacy from prominent figures, including the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu. Bamidele stated that the under-representation of women in political institutions required deliberate legislative intervention. He said the proposed reform was intended to strengthen democratic inclusion and ensure that women’s interests received adequate attention in the formulation of public policies. He stated, “The special seat initiative is not a partisan endeavour. It is a historic imperative. “The rationale is anchored on a simple, yet profound, principle of constitutional law: the foundational precept of representative democracy. The senate leader also highlighted the need for legislative interventions to protect women, children, and other vulnerable groups, particularly in the areas of healthcare, education, and social protection. He maintained that government had a responsibility to provide adequate safeguards where prevailing market conditions, cultural practices, and institutional weaknesses failed to protect vulnerable citizens. On access to justice, Bamidele insisted that the country’s legal framework must respond effectively to emerging threats against women and children, stressing that justice should not remain a constitutional promise or a provision in the statute books. “Rather, it must be accessible, affordable, timely, and effective,” he said. Bamidele added, “A woman who suffers domestic violence must be able to seek protection without intimidation or social condemnation. A child who experiences abuse must be heard, protected from further harm, and provided with appropriate support. FIDA, Ekiti State Chapter, chaired by Mrs. Ayobami Olowoyo-Richards, organised the Law Week with the theme, “Justice in a Changing World: Responding to New Challenges Affecting Women and Children.” The event was attended by Chairman of House of Representatives Committee on Information and National Orientation, Hon. Steve Fatoba; Speaker of Ekiti State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Adeoye Aribasoye; and other dignitaries. 尼日利亚国民议会提议在参议院和众议院增设74个专门保留给女性的席位，以作为解决尼日利亚政治代表中性别失衡问题持续努力的一部分。该提案还规定在尼日利亚36个州议会各为女性增设3个席位，旨在扩大女性对立法决策的参与，同时不取消现有选区，也不取代现任议员。

参议院领袖奥佩耶米·巴米德莱参议员周一在由国际女律师联合会（FIDA）埃基蒂州分会组织的2026年法律周活动上公布了这项提案。巴米德莱同时担任参议院1999年宪法审查委员会副主席。他说，这项提案是第十届国民议会正在进行的宪法修订工作的一部分。他解释说，拟议安排将在参议院增加37个席位，在众议院再增加37个席位，确保联邦每个州及联邦首都领地在两院中各增加一名代表。

据他介绍，拟议中的专门席位旨在让女性有更多机会担任民选职位和参与决策平台，尤其是考虑到女性在尼日利亚立法机构中的代表比例历来较低。巴米德莱透露，宪法审查委员会还建议在每个州议会为女性增加3个席位。他强调，拟议席位将专门保留给女性，不会影响现有选区，也不会取代任何在任议员。

他还说，该安排将实施16年，涵盖4个选举周期，之后将进行全面审查。巴米德莱解释道：“这项安排拟实施16年，即4个选举周期，之后再进行全面审查。这是一项日落条款，旨在确保制度的可持续性，并为更具包容性的政治文化实现自然发展留出空间。”

这位参议院领袖表示有信心，该提案将获得必要的立法支持，尤其是各州议会的支持，因为根据宪法，完成修宪程序必须取得州议会的同意。他说：“我们正在积极且有策略地与各州议会沟通，因为取得它们的同意是推动这项改革实现的宪法必要条件。”

巴米德莱将拟议的专门席位描述为一项根本性的民主改革，而非党派政治行动。他表示，如果将相当大比例的人口排除在立法决策之外，代表制民主就无法有效运作。他说，这项倡议是在广泛征询意见和凝聚共识后提出的；第十届国民议会特意提前启动宪法审查程序，以便留出充足时间进行审查并扩大利益相关方的参与。他还表示，第一夫人奥卢雷米·蒂努布参议员等知名人士的倡导，也加强了第十届国民议会对这项倡议的投入。

巴米德莱指出，女性在政治机构中代表不足，需要立法机关有意采取干预措施。他说，拟议改革旨在加强民主包容性，确保女性利益在公共政策制定中得到充分关注。他表示：“专门席位倡议不是党派行为，而是历史的必然要求。其依据植根于宪法-law的一项简单却深刻的原则：代表制民主的基本原则。”

这位参议院领袖还强调，需要通过立法干预保护女性、儿童及其他弱势群体，尤其是在医疗保健、教育和社会保护等领域。他坚持认为，当 prevailing 市场状况、文化习俗和制度缺陷未能保护弱势公民时，政府有责任提供充分保障。

在司法可及性方面，巴米德莱坚称，该国法律框架必须有效应对针对女性和儿童的新兴威胁，强调司法不应仅仅停留在宪法承诺或法条之中。他说：“相反，司法必须易于获得、价格可负担、及时且有效。”巴米德莱补充道：“遭受家庭暴力的女性必须能够寻求保护，而不受恐吓或社会谴责。遭受虐待的儿童必须有机会表达意见，受到保护以免进一步受到伤害，并获得适当支持。”

由阿约巴米·奥洛约-理查兹夫人担任主席的FIDA埃基蒂州分会组织了本届法律周活动，主题为“变化世界中的司法：应对影响女性和儿童的新挑战”。众议院信息与国家导向委员会主席史蒂夫·法托巴阁下、埃基蒂州议会议长阿德奥耶·阿里巴索耶阁下及其他贵宾出席了活动。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/n.body: The Commission Chief Executive, Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), Mrs. Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, yesterday told investors that Nigeria offers a stable climate amid the global energy tension. Eyesan therefore urged investors to look towards Nigeria by taking advantage of the 2026 Licensing Round which has 40 oil and gas blocks on offer. She also disclosed that the licensing round portal will officially open on November 20, 2026. The NUPRC boss said this during a roundtable discussion titled: ‘Energy Sovereignty in an Interconnected World: Aligning National Priorities, Markets and Global Security’ at the 2026 ADIPEC Exhibition and Conference in Abu Dhabi on Monday, November 2, 2026. A statement by the NUPRC Head of Media and Corporate Communications, Eniola Akinkuotu, quoted Eyesan as saying that with a very attractive fiscal framework for investors, she was expecting to see even more interest in the new licensing round. She said: “We are expecting investors to turn to Nigeria. We are going in for another licensing round and we will be launching our bid portal on November 20. We expect to see interested investors because the environment is a lot more competitive. “We have set a very attractive fiscal framework for investors. The entire environment is a lot more secure. We have been able to manage costs with a lot of incentives for investors and we expect to see investors take up the offer when we open the portal.” The NUPRC chief noted that since the passing of the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) in 2021 as well as the executive orders signed by President Bola Tinubu, Nigeria has seen an improvement in its investment climate. Eyesan stated that between 2021 and 2026, the NUPRC had held at least four successful licensing rounds which had brought in more investments into the country. This, she said, is a departure from the pre-PIA era where licensing rounds were not frequent. The NURPC chief executive said that Nigeria possesses huge energy potential as it sits on 215 Trillion Cubic Feet (TCF) of gas, but could barely produce 7 Billion Cubic Feet (BCF) daily. According to her, the situation presents an opportunity to investors, especially as key gas infrastructure projects are in the pipeline. She added: “The stars are already aligned. For gas infrastructure we just completed very major infrastructure projects that will unlock gas supply in the country and the sub-region. “We talk about two major projects on the drawing board to move gas through the Nigeria-Morocco Atlantic Gas Pipeline and Trans-Sahara Gas Pipeline. Again, this gas will go somewhere in Europe and will also meet regional demands. So, Nigeria is positioned to meet not just domestic supply,” the CCE stated. Eyesan maintained that with many countries discovering petroleum resources, the race for investments has become even more competitive. She said Nigeria was already ahead of the game as it had made certain modifications in order to attract the right capital. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/n.title_zh: 尼日利亚上游石油生产监管委员会：2026年40个油气区块竞标门户将在17天后开放
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/n.body_zh: 尼日利亚上游石油监管委员会（NUPRC）委员会首席执行官奥里特塞米耶瓦·艾桑夫人昨日告诉投资者，在全球能源局势紧张之际，尼日利亚具备稳定的投资环境。因此，艾桑敦促投资者把握2026年许可轮次提供的机会，该轮次共有40个石油和天然气区块可供申领。她还透露，许可轮次申领门户将于2026年11月20日正式开放。NUPRC负责人是在2026年11月2日星期一于阿布扎比举行的2026年ADIPEC展览与会议上，围绕“互联世界中的能源主权：协调国家优先事项、市场与全球安全”这一主题的圆桌讨论中作出上述表态的。NUPRC媒体与公司传播主管埃尼奥拉·阿金库图发表声明，引述艾桑的话说，凭借对投资者极具吸引力的财政框架，她预计新一轮许可将获得更多关注。她说：“我们期待投资者转向尼日利亚。我们将启动另一轮许可，并于11月20日推出申领门户。由于这里的竞争环境更加激烈，我们预计会吸引有意投资的投资者。我们为投资者制定了极具吸引力的财政框架。整个环境的安全性和稳定性都大幅提高。我们通过提供多项激励措施来控制成本，并预计门户开放后会有投资者接受这些条件。”NUPRC负责人指出，自2021年《石油产业法》（PIA）通过以及总统博拉·蒂努布签署行政命令以来，尼日利亚的投资环境有所改善。艾桑表示，2021年至2026年间，NUPRC至少举办了4轮成功的许可招标，为该国引入了更多投资。她说，这与PIA实施前许可轮次举办频率不高的时期不同。NURPC首席执行官表示，尼日利亚拥有巨大的能源潜力，坐拥215万亿立方英尺（TCF）天然气储量，但目前的日产量勉强达到70亿立方英尺（BCF）。据她介绍，鉴于关键天然气基础设施项目正在推进，这一现状为投资者提供了机遇。她补充说：“各项条件已经具备。就天然气基础设施而言，我们刚刚完成了若干重大基础设施项目，这些项目将释放尼日利亚及该地区的天然气供应。我们正在规划两个重大项目，通过尼日利亚—摩洛哥大西洋天然气管道和跨撒哈拉天然气管道输送天然气。这些天然气还将输往欧洲，以满足区域需求。因此，尼日利亚已具备满足国内需求乃至更广泛需求的供应能力。”这位委员会首席执行官强调，随着许多国家发现石油资源，投资竞争愈发激烈。她说，尼日利亚已经抢占先机，为吸引优质资本作出了一些调整。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创办，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，社址位于尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕溪路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都 Territory及世界各地设有办事处。作为尼日利亚最权威的新闻媒体，THISDAY通过全平台服务政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶层，同时为有抱负者和千禧一代提供新思想、文化与技术的交汇点。该报秉持公共信托精神，致力于追求真相与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育和社区等议题，直面人民与社会的交汇点。您可以给我们发送电子邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/curr.summary: Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Money and Credit Statistics, also showed that currency outside banks increased by 10.3 per cent year-on-year from N4.465 trillion in September 2025 to N4.923 trillion in September 2026. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/curr.summary_zh: 尼日利亚中央银行（CBN）《货币与信贷统计》数据显示，银行体系外流通的货币同比增加10.3%，从2025年9月的4.465万亿奈拉增至2026年9月的4.923万亿奈拉。数据细分显示，银行体系外流通的货币从2023年9月的2.416万亿奈拉增至2024年9月的4.016万亿奈拉，增幅为66.2%。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/curr.body: •Demand deposits climb 71% •Analysts highlight cash dependence, financial inclusion challenges Currency held outside the banking system by Nigerians rose by 103.8 per cent to N4.923 trillion in September 2026 from N2.416 trillion in September 2023, highlighting the persistent demand for physical cash despite the expansion of electronic payment channels in the country. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Money and Credit Statistics, also showed that currency outside banks increased by 10.3 per cent year-on-year from N4.465 trillion in September 2025 to N4.923 trillion in September 2026. The figures indicate that cash held outside the banking system has more than doubled in three years, reflecting the scale of currency demand within the economy and the challenges facing efforts to deepen the use of formal banking and electronic payment systems. A breakdown of the data showed that currency outside banks increased by 66.2 per cent from N2.416 trillion in September 2023 to N4.016 trillion in September 2024. The figure subsequently rose to N4.465 trillion in September 2025, an increase of 11.2 per cent from the corresponding period in 2024, before climbing further to N4.923 trillion in September 2026. According to analysts, the latest increase indicates that the preference for cash transactions remains significant, notwithstanding the growing adoption of mobile banking, electronic transfers, point-of-sale terminals and other digital payment platforms. Meanwhile, demand deposits in the banking system increased by 70.8 per cent to N39.124 trillion in September 2026 from N22.903 trillion in September 2023. The CBN data showed that demand deposits rose to N31.842 trillion in September 2024, representing an increase of 39.0 per cent against the corresponding period in 2023. The figure climbed further to N34.642 trillion in September 2025, an increase of 8.8 per cent year-on-year, before rising to N39.124 trillion in September 2026, representing a 12.9 per cent increase over September 2025. The growth in demand deposits indicates an expansion in funds held in bank accounts that are generally accessible for payments and withdrawals on demand. Reacting to this data, Clifford Egbomeade, Economic and Communications expert, said: “The simultaneous increase in demand deposits and currency outside banks points to the coexistence of formal banking balances and substantial demand for physical cash in Nigeria’s payment system. ‘‘However, the two indicators measure different components of monetary activity. Demand deposits represent bank-account balances, while currency outside banks represents cash held outside the banking system. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/curr.title_zh: 银行外流通货币三年增长104%
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/curr.body_zh: •活期存款增长71% •分析人士指出对现金的依赖及普惠金融挑战 尼日利亚人存放在银行体系外的现金从2023年9月的2.416万亿奈拉增至2026年9月的4.923万亿奈拉，增幅为103.8%，尽管该国电子支付渠道不断扩展，实体现金需求依然旺盛。尼日利亚中央银行CBN的货币与信贷统计数据显示，银行体系外流通的货币从2025年9月的4.465万亿奈拉增至2026年9月的4.923万亿奈拉，同比增幅为10.3%。这些数字表明，银行体系外持有的现金在3年内增长了一倍以上，反映出经济体内现金需求的规模，以及深化正规银行和电子支付系统使用所面临的挑战。数据明细显示，银行体系外流通的货币从2023年9月的2.416万亿奈拉增至2024年9月的4.016万亿奈拉，增幅为66.2%。此后，这一数字在2025年9月升至4.465万亿奈拉，较2024年同期增长11.2%，随后在2026年9月进一步升至4.923万亿奈拉。分析人士称，最新增幅表明，尽管移动银行、电子转账、销售终端及其他数字支付平台的采用率不断提高，人们对现金交易的偏好仍然十分显著。与此同时，银行体系内的活期存款从2023年9月的22.903万亿奈拉增至2026年9月的39.124万亿奈拉，增幅为70.8%。CBN数据显示，活期存款在2024年9月升至31.842万亿奈拉，较2023年同期增长39.0%。这一数字在2025年9月进一步升至34.642万亿奈拉，同比增长8.8%，随后在2026年9月升至39.124万亿奈拉，较2025年9月增长12.9%。活期存款的增长表明，银行账户中的资金规模扩大，这些资金通常可按需用于支付和提取。针对这组数据，经济与传播问题专家Clifford Egbomeade表示：“活期存款与银行体系外流通的货币同步增长，表明尼日利亚支付体系中正规银行余额与对实体现金的大量需求并存。不过，这两个指标衡量的是货币活动的不同组成部分。活期存款代表银行账户余额，而银行体系外流通的货币则代表存放在银行体系外的现金。此处表达的意见并不反映Vanguard报纸或其任何员工的观点

https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body: India’s manufacturing sector activity lost some growth momentum in October compared to September as output and new orders increased only marginally, according to HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) data released by S&P Global on Monday. The headline figure, the manufacturing PMI — tracks factory conditions based on new orders, output, employment, suppliers’ delivery time, and stock of purchases — stood at 54.7 in October, compared to 55.1 in September. To be sure, manufacturing activity remained in expansion, as the index stood above 50. “India’s manufacturing PMI softened to 54.7 in October from 55.1 in the previous month, but remained firmly in expansionary territory and above its long-run average,” said Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC. New business increased in October reflecting sustained demand for manufacturing goods. Growth softened marginally from September, which recorded a seven-month high, though it remained strong by historical standards. Firms cited favourable demand trends, new client wins and successful marketing campaigns for the growth. International orders increased at the fastest rate in six months and contributed to the index’s expansion. Firms reported gains from Bangladesh, Canada, Indonesia, Nepal, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, the UK, US and the UAE. Output increased at a sharp rate backed by rising sales and new product releases, which exceeded its long-run average. Though growth slowed compared to September as intermediate goods activity softened. However, intermediate goods still led the expansion. Across all three broad areas of manufacturing tracked by the PMI survey, cost pressures eased. Although firms observed higher prices for energy and certain materials, overall inflation was the lowest since February. As a result, firms raised selling prices only slightly to protect margins. Employment increased as new orders led to higher production requirements and rising workloads. Outstanding business volumes against the orders received increased, but the pace of accumulation was very slow. Finished goods stocks rose sharply, with firms reporting measured efforts to accommodate buoyant demand and prevent shortages. Input inventories also increased, leading the rate of accumulation to reach an eight-month high. “Producers also increased input inventories to the greatest extent in eight months, building precautionary buffers to mitigate potential shortages and meet rising production requirements amid a volatile global environment,” she added. Business confidence weakened in October compared to September and remained below its long-run average. Around 18% of firms expect higher output in the next twelve months, while others remained neutral. Firms that remained optimistic credited this to new client enquiries and demand for industrial automation and technology solutions
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.title_zh: 印度制造业增长势头在10月减弱
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body_zh: 标普全球周一发布的汇丰印度制造业采购经理指数（PMI）数据显示，与9月相比，印度制造业活动在10月失去部分增长动力，产出和新订单仅略有增加。制造业PMI这一 headline 数据根据新订单、产出、就业、供应商交付时间和采购库存追踪工厂状况，10月为54.7，9月为55.1。尽管如此，制造业活动仍处于扩张区间，因为该指数高于50。汇丰首席印度经济学家Pranjul Bhandari表示：“印度制造业PMI从上月55.1降至10月的54.7，但仍稳稳处于扩张区间，并高于其长期平均水平。”10月新业务增加，反映出对制成品的需求持续旺盛。增速较9月略有放缓，9月曾录得七个月高点，不过按历史标准衡量仍表现强劲。企业称，有利的需求趋势、新客户订单以及成功的营销活动推动了增长。国际订单增速达到六个月最快，并推动指数上升。企业报告来自孟加拉国、加拿大、印度尼西亚、尼泊尔、阿曼、沙特阿拉伯、斯里兰卡、英国、美国和阿联酋的收益增加。在销售增长和新产品推出的带动下，产出以较快速度增长，增幅超过其长期平均水平。尽管中间品活动走软使增速较9月放缓，但中间品仍引领扩张。在PMI调查追踪的制造业三大领域，成本压力均有所缓解。尽管企业观察到能源和某些材料价格上涨，但整体通胀率为2月以来最低。因此，企业仅略微提高销售价格，以保护利润率。新订单带来更高的生产需求和上升的工作量，推动就业增加。未完成业务量相对于所收到订单有所增加，但积压速度非常缓慢。成品库存大幅上升，企业报告称正适度努力满足旺盛需求并防止短缺。投入库存也有所增加，积累速度达到八个月高点。她补充道：“生产商还以八个月来最大幅度增加投入库存，建立预防性库存缓冲，以缓解潜在短缺，并在全球环境动荡之际满足不断上升的生产需求。”10月商业信心较9月减弱，仍低于其长期平均水平。约18%的企业预计未来十二个月产出将增加，其余企业则持中性态度。保持乐观的企业将原因归为新客户询盘以及对工业自动化和技术解决方案的需求

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/2027.summary: ABUJA — President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, has expressed confidence that Akwa Ibom State will deliver the highest number of votes for President Bola Tinubu in the South-South region in the 2027 presidential election. “From what I have seen here today, Akwa Ibom State will give Mr President the highest number of votes in the South-South region,” he said.
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/2027.summary_zh: 阿布贾——参议院议长戈德斯维尔·阿kpabio参议员表示有信心，阿夸伊博姆州将在2027年总统选举中为总统博拉·蒂努布在东南部地区赢得最高票数。他说：“从今天我在此看到的情况来看，阿夸伊博姆州将在东南部地区给总统先生投下最高票数。”
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/2027.body: ABUJA — President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, has expressed confidence that Akwa Ibom State will deliver the highest number of votes for President Bola Tinubu in the South-South region in the 2027 presidential election. Akpabio made the declaration on Sunday during a special church service at the International Christian Worship Centre, Uyo, organised to dedicate the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 election campaigns to God. In a statement by his Special Assistant on Media, Jackson Udom, the Senate President said Akwa Ibom indigenes, particularly APC members, must close ranks and present a united front to ensure the party’s success at the polls. He said the state had a responsibility to reciprocate the support President Tinubu had given him by mobilising votes for the President. According to him, the support of Tinubu contributed to his emergence as Senate President, making him the number three citizen in the country. “Whether you like him or not, he is there today. The only way to thank Mr President for that support is to give him all our votes. “From what I have seen here today, Akwa Ibom State will give Mr President the highest number of votes in the South-South region,” he said. In an address titled, “One Family, One Destiny, One Akwa Ibom Under God”, Akpabio said while the people acknowledged God’s sovereignty over their individual and collective destinies, they must also uphold righteousness, justice and mercy. He described Akwa Ibom as a Nigerian success story, attributing its progress to purposeful leadership, peace and development. The Senate President said development should not be measured only by roads and buildings but also by the bridges built between people and the hope restored in their lives. He urged political leaders and party members to sustain the state’s progress and ensure that its future achievements surpassed those already recorded. On party unity, Akpabio cautioned against divisions between old and new members of the APC, insisting that all members should be treated equally. “In the APC family, there should be no aborigines and no newcomers; no landlords and no tenants; no first-class members and no second-class members. There should be only one big family, united by a common purpose and a shared responsibility,” he said. Using a biblical reference from John 14:2, he said there was room for everyone in the party, regardless of when they joined or their political standing. He added that political ambitions should not override the welfare of the people, urging party members to conduct their campaigns in ways that respect human dignity. Akpabio further said the development of Akwa Ibom was inseparable from the progress of Nigeria, stressing that the state could not remain indifferent to insecurity and hardship in other parts of the country. “Nigeria is not merely the nation to which Akwa Ibom belongs; it is the larger destiny to which Akwa Ibom contributes,” he said. Earlier, Governor Umo Eno thanked the people for their support during the last election and appealed for increased support for Tinubu, Akpabio, himself and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections. Eno also pledged to continue serving the people with the fear of God if given another mandate. Comments expressed here do not reflect the opinions of Vanguard newspapers or any employee thereof

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/2027.body_zh: 阿布贾——参议院议长戈德斯威尔·阿kpabio表示，他确信在2027年总统选举中，阿夸伊博姆州将在南南地区为博拉·蒂努布总统争取到最多选票。阿kpabio于周日在乌约国际基督教敬拜中心举行的特别礼拜活动上作出上述表态。此次活动旨在将全进步大会党（APC）2027年选举竞选活动献给上帝。参议院议长在接受其媒体特别助理杰克逊·乌多姆的声明中表示，阿夸伊博姆本地居民，尤其是APC成员，必须团结一致，形成统一阵线，以确保该党在选举中获胜。他说，该州有责任通过动员选票支持蒂努布总统，以回报蒂努布总统此前对他的支持。据他所说，蒂努布的支持促成了他成为参议院议长，使他成为尼日利亚国内地位第三高的公民。他说：“无论你喜欢他还是不喜欢他，他今天都在那里。报答总统先生这种支持的唯一方式，就是把我们的全部选票投给他。‘从今天我在这里看到的情况来看，阿夸伊博姆州将在南南地区为总统先生投出最多选票。’”在一篇题为《在上帝之下，一个家庭、一个命运、一个阿夸伊博姆》的讲话中，阿kpabio表示，尽管民众承认上帝主宰着他们个人和集体的命运，但他们也必须秉持正直、公正和怜悯。他把阿夸伊博姆描述为尼日利亚的一个成功范例，并将该州的进步归功于有明确目标的领导、和平与发展。参议院议长表示，衡量发展不能只看道路和建筑物，还要看人与人之间架起的桥梁，以及他们生活中重新燃起的希望。他敦促政治领导人和党内成员维持该州的发展势头，确保其未来成就超越已经取得的成果。在谈及党内团结时，阿kpabio警告不要在APC新老成员之间制造分裂，坚持所有成员都应受到平等对待。他说：“在APC这个大家庭里，不应有原住民和新来者，不应有房东和租客，也不应有一等成员和二等成员。这个大家庭应当只有一个，大家由共同的目标和共同的责任团结在一起。”他引用《约翰福音》14章2节指出，无论党员何时加入该党，也无论其政治地位如何，党内都有容纳每个人的空间。他补充说，政治野心不应凌驾于民众福祉之上，并敦促党内成员以尊重人的尊严的方式开展竞选活动。Akpabio还表示，阿夸伊博姆的发展与尼日利亚的进步密不可分，强调该州不能对尼日利亚其他地区的不安全状况和困境无动于衷。他说：“尼日利亚不仅仅是阿夸伊博姆所属的国家；它也是阿夸伊博姆为之作出贡献的更大命运。”此前，州长乌莫·埃诺感谢民众在上次选举期间给予的支持，并呼吁在2027年选举中进一步支持蒂努布、阿kpabio、他本人以及其他APC候选人。埃诺还承诺，如果再次获得授权，他将继续怀着对上帝的敬畏服务民众。此处发表的评论不代表《Vanguard》报及其任何员工的观点

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body: Governor Francis Nwifuru of Ebonyi State says his administration has forwarded an executive bill to the state House of Assembly to make kidnapping a capital offence punishable by death without an option of alternative punishment. Mr Nwifuru said this on Friday during the funeral of the slain traditional ruler of Ndufu-Alike Community in Ikwo Local Government Area, Francis Igwe, Vanguard reported . “This should serve as a deterrent to those planning a kidnapping, whether for political reasons or otherwise,” the governor said. Mr Igwe, father of the immediate past Deputy Governor of Ebonyi State, Kelechi Igwe, was abducted on 1 March 1 while on his way to church. Mr Nwifuru, while speaking at the traditional ruler’s funeral, decried the moral deterioration among Nigerian youths. “I am worried about our present-day youths taking up leadership positions tomorrow. Some of our youths are not well informed, and they act so irrationally. “I am concerned because, with some of their attitudinal dispositions, there seems to be no future for our youths. “The youths need to have a rethink concerning certain actions of theirs, especially as concerns their attitudes towards community leaders,” he said. “They should desist from treating their leaders as holders of their destinies.” Mr Nwifuru vowed to implement any court decision against those arrested over the traditional ruler’s murder, stressing that the proposed legislation was intended to deter kidnapping in the state. He maintained that the traditional ruler’s murder should be the last of such incidents in Ikwo and other parts of the state. The governor described the late traditional ruler as “a forthright, vocal and astute parliamentarian” who represented his people effectively in the old Anambra State. He said the traditional ruler attracted development projects to his community, including the popular Folk Technical College, which has produced prominent Nigerians. In their tributes, former governors of the state, Sam Egwu and Martin Elechi, as well as former Senate President, Pius Anyim, described the deceased as a statesman, peacemaker, renowned educationist, administrator and passionate leader who left enduring legacies. They urged the family and the Ikwo people to take solace in his contributions to society. Speaking in his tribute, the slain traditional ruler’s first son and former deputy governor, Kelechi, described his father as a devoted family man and role model who guided him on family life, religion, politics and culture. He said the circumstances surrounding his father’s death remained difficult for the family to comprehend. The former deputy governor said the family was confident that the legacy of the slain traditional ruler would endure for generations to come. The offence attracts severe penalties, including life imprisonment and, in certain circumstances, the death penalty. Criminal Code Act and the Terrorism (Prevention and Prohibition) Act 2022 are the two principal laws that outlaw kidnapping and hostage taking. While the Criminal Code Act prescribes imprisonment of up to 10 years, the Terrorism (Prevention and Prohibition) Act 2022, which addresses the offence in the context of terrorism, prescribes severe punishment, including death, where the offence resulted in the death of a victim. However, the punishment for kidnappings varies across the states in the country. PREMIUM TIMES reports that the applicable legislation on kidnapping is the Ebonyi State Internal Security Enforcement and Other Related Matters Law, 2009 (Cap. 55, Vol. 2)
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.title_zh: 州长要求对绑架者判处死刑，并将法案提交州议会
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body_zh: 埃博尼州州长弗朗西斯·恩维富鲁表示，其政府已向该州众议院提交一项行政法案，拟将绑架定为可判处死刑且不得以其他刑罚替代的资本罪行。恩维富鲁先生于周五在伊克沃地方政府辖区恩杜富-阿利克社区遇害传统酋长弗朗西斯·伊格韦的葬礼上说了这番话，《Vanguard》报道称。州长说：“无论出于政治目的还是其他原因，这都应当对那些策划绑架的人形成威慑。”伊格韦先生是埃博尼州前副州长凯莱奇·伊格韦的父亲，他于3月1日前往教堂途中遭绑架。恩维富鲁州长在传统酋长葬礼上发言时，谴责了尼日利亚年轻人之间的道德滑坡。他说：“我担心我们当代的年轻人明天担任领导职务时，会出现一些问题。我们的一些年轻人见识不足，行事又十分不理性。令我担忧的是，从他们某些态度倾向来看，我们年轻人似乎没有未来。年轻人需要重新思考自己的某些行为，尤其是对社区领袖的态度，”他说，“他们不应再把领袖视决定自己命运的人。”恩维富鲁先生誓言执行法院针对因谋杀传统酋长而被捕者的任何裁决，并强调拟议立法的目的在于遏制该州的绑架行为。他坚持认为，传统酋长遇害应当成为伊克沃及该州其他地区此类事件中的最后一例。州长称已故传统酋长是“一位正直、敢于发声且精明的议员”，曾在旧阿南布拉州有效代表民众。他还 said，传统酋长为所在社区吸引了发展项目，其中包括颇受欢迎的民间技术学院，该学院培养出了多位尼日利亚杰出人物。在悼词中，该州前州长萨姆·埃格沃、马丁·埃莱奇以及前参议院议长皮乌斯·阿尼姆称逝者是一位政治家、和平缔造者、知名教育家、行政管理者和充满热情的领袖，留下了 enduring legacies。他们敦促其家人和伊克沃民众从他为社会作出的贡献中寻求慰藉。在悼词中，遇害传统酋长的长子、前副州长凯莱奇称父亲是一位忠于家庭的楷模，在家庭生活、宗教、政治和文化方面都给予他指导。他说，围绕父亲死亡的具体情况，家人至今仍难以理解。这位前副州长表示，家人相信，遇害传统酋长留下的精神遗产将世代延续。该罪行的刑罚严厉，包括无期徒刑，在某些情况下还可判处死刑。《刑法典》和《2022年恐怖主义预防与禁止法》是禁止绑架和劫持人质的两部主要法律。《刑法典》规定最高可判处10年监禁，而从恐怖主义背景下处理该罪行的《2022年恐怖主义预防与禁止法》则规定严厉处罚，如果犯罪行为导致受害者死亡，可判处死刑。不过，全国各州对绑架罪的处罚规定有所不同。《PREMIUM TIMES》报道称，适用于绑架案的立法是《2009年埃博尼州内部安全执法及其他相关事项法》（Cap. 55, Vol. 2）

https://aa.com.tr/en/world/nato-allies-f.body: The diplomats, who spoke on condition of anonymity, expressed concern that congressional constraints on Trump's domestic agenda could prompt him to pursue more assertive foreign policy measures. They said Trump could withdraw thousands more US troops from Europe, with a review of American forces stationed on the continent expected by December. Trump could also reduce US contributions to NATO's common funding, restrict the alliance-backed PURL arms-buying scheme for Ukraine or deepen ties with Russia, according to the report. Oana Lungescu, a former NATO official and distinguished fellow at the Royal United Services Institute, warned that Washington could link its military presence in Europe to European acceptance of a US-backed peace deal for Ukraine. She said treating troop deployments, Ukraine and Europe's security arrangements as elements of a broader agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin could create a dangerous situation for European security. She cited NATO allies' agreement to increase defense spending and Trump's efforts to end Russia's war in Ukraine, while reiterating his criticism of allies over the war in Iran. Montenegrin Defense Minister Dragan Krapovic offered a more cautious assessment, noting that previous predictions of a US withdrawal from NATO had not materialized. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/nass.summary: ADO-EKITI — Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, has said the 10th National Assembly is committed to removing barriers limiting women’s participation in governance through a proposed constitutional amendment seeking special seats for women in the National and State Houses of Assembly.
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/nass.summary_zh: ADO-EKITI——参议院领袖奥佩耶米·巴米德莱参议员表示，第10届全国大会致力于通过拟议的宪法修正案清除阻碍女性参与治理的障碍，寻求在全国议会和州议会为女性设置专门席位。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/nass.body: ADO-EKITI — Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, has said the 10th National Assembly is committed to removing barriers limiting women’s participation in governance through a proposed constitutional amendment seeking special seats for women in the National and State Houses of Assembly. Bamidele, who represents Ekiti Central Senatorial District, said the proposed legislation was designed to address the persistent under-representation of women in Nigeria’s political institutions and ensure their participation in decisions affecting the country. He spoke as a guest speaker at the 2026 Law Week of the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA), Ekiti State Chapter, held in Ado-Ekiti, with the theme, “Justice in a Changing World: Responding to New Challenges Affecting Women and Children”. The Senate Leader said the proposed constitutional alteration would create 37 additional seats in the Senate and 37 in the House of Representatives, with one seat reserved for women in each state and the Federal Capital Territory. He added that the proposal also provided for three additional seats in each State House of Assembly, without displacing existing legislative seats. According to him, the arrangement is proposed to run for 16 years, covering four electoral cycles, after which its impact would be reviewed. Describing the initiative as a historic intervention rather than a partisan project, Bamidele said a democracy that excluded a significant proportion of its population from decision-making could not claim to be fully representative. He disclosed that the National Assembly had commenced engagements with State Houses of Assembly to secure the constitutionally required concurrence for the proposed amendment. He said the process was being pursued through extensive consultations and consensus-building. Bamidele, who commended the advocacy of the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, said the 10th Assembly was determined to address historical gaps in women’s political representation. The lawmaker also identified globalisation, artificial intelligence, digitalisation, insecurity, economic instability and climate change as factors creating new challenges for women and children. He said women continued to face gender-based violence, economic exclusion, discrimination and inadequate healthcare, while children remained vulnerable to sexual abuse, trafficking, child labour, early marriage, malnutrition, educational deprivation and digital exploitation. He noted that poverty, unemployment, inadequate social protection, educational inequalities, social stigma and weak enforcement of existing laws had further compounded the challenges. Bamidele maintained that protecting women and children was not merely a humanitarian responsibility but a constitutional obligation and a critical investment in national development, economic productivity and social stability. He also highlighted legislative interventions of the 10th Assembly, including the four Tax Reform Acts of 2025, which he said exempted sanitary products, baby diapers and other essential products for women and children from Value Added Tax. He described the measure as a social justice intervention aimed at reducing the financial burden on low-income women and families. The Senate Leader urged FIDA to deepen its engagement with the National Assembly and other relevant institutions by identifying gaps in existing laws, proposing reforms and ensuring that government policies and budgetary provisions translated into tangible benefits for vulnerable Nigerians. He also challenged the organisation to hold the legislature accountable for implementing its commitments, particularly the proposed special seats for women and adequate funding for child protection, women’s healthcare and gender empowerment programmes. “A democracy that systematically excludes over half of its population from the decision-making tables that determine their future is, at best, a flawed democracy and, at worst, a veiled oligarchy. “The law is only as good as its implementation. Hold us accountable. Demand that the Special Seats Bill becomes law. Demand that appropriations for child protection and women’s health are not just passed, but released and utilised,” he said. In her keynote address, the Vice-Chancellor of Afe Babalola University, Ado-Ekiti, Professor Smaranda Olarinde, called for stronger legal and institutional frameworks to protect women and children against emerging forms of abuse, particularly those enabled by technology and economic vulnerabilities. Olarinde said the growing use of artificial intelligence and digital platforms had created new threats, including cyberstalking, online harassment, deepfake images, impersonation and the exploitation of children. She called for stronger collaboration among government, the judiciary, law enforcement agencies, universities, religious and traditional leaders, the media and civil society organisations to tackle gender-based violence and child abuse. The vice-chancellor also urged FIDA to move beyond advocacy to measurable outcomes, proposing a collaborative Women and Children Access to Justice Action Framework to improve legal protection, digital safety and support for survivors. In his remarks, the Chief Judge of Ekiti State, Justice Ogunmoye, commended FIDA for selecting Bamidele to deliver the lecture, describing him as well placed to address emerging issues requiring legislative and policy reforms to protect women and children. Earlier, the Chairperson of FIDA, Ekiti State chapter, Ayobami Olowoyo-Richards, said the organisation would remain committed to promoting, protecting and preserving the rights of women and children. She said changing realities continued to present new challenges to their safety, dignity and fundamental rights, requiring stronger laws, institutions and collective responses to ensure access to justice. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/nass.title_zh: 尼日利亚国民议会承诺提高女性参与度
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/nass.body_zh: 阿多埃基蒂——参议院领袖、参议员奥佩耶米·巴米德莱表示，第10届全国大会致力于通过拟议的宪法修正案消除阻碍女性参与治理的障碍，寻求在国民议会和州议会为女性设立专属议席。巴米德莱代表埃基蒂中央选区参议员区，他说，拟议立法旨在解决女性在尼日利亚政治机构中长期代表不足的问题，并确保女性参与影响国家的各项决策。他是在阿多埃基蒂举行的2026年国际女律师联合会（FIDA）埃基蒂州分会法律周活动上作为嘉宾发言的，主题为“变化中的世界中的正义：应对影响妇女和儿童的新挑战”。参议院领袖表示，拟议的宪法修订将在参议院增设37个议席，在众议院增设37个议席，每个州和联邦首都直辖区各保留1个女性席位。他补充说，该提案还将为每个州议会增加3个席位，而不会挤占现有立法席位。据他介绍，这项安排拟实施16年，涵盖4个选举周期，之后将对其影响进行评估。巴米德莱称，这项倡议是一项历史性干预，而非党派项目；如果一个民主制度将相当大比例的人口排除在决策之外，就不能声称自己具有充分的代表性。他透露，全国大会已开始与各州议会接洽，以取得宪法要求的修正案同意。他说，这一进程正通过广泛磋商和凝聚共识推进。巴米德莱赞扬了第一夫人、参议员奥卢雷米·蒂努布的倡导工作，并表示第10届大会决心弥合女性政治代表方面的历史差距。这位议员还指出，全球化、人工智能、数字化、不安全局势、经济不稳定和气候变化正在给妇女和儿童带来新的挑战。他说，妇女仍面临基于性别的暴力、经济排斥、歧视和医疗保障不足，而儿童仍易遭受性虐待、人口贩运、童工、早婚、营养不良、教育匮乏和数字剥削。他指出，贫困、失业、社会保障不足、教育不平等、社会污名和现有法律执行不力进一步加剧了这些挑战。巴米德莱坚持认为，保护妇女和儿童不仅是人道主义责任，也是宪法义务，更是促进国家发展、经济生产力和社会稳定的关键投资。他还强调了第10届大会采取的立法措施，包括2025年的4部《税制改革法》，据他说，这些法律免除了卫生用品、婴儿纸尿裤和其他妇女及儿童必需品的产品增值税。他称，这项措施是一项社会公正干预，旨在减轻低收入妇女和家庭的经济负担。参议院领袖敦促FIDA加强与全国大会及其他相关机构的合作，找出现有法律中的缺口、提出改革建议，并确保政府政策和预算安排转化为弱势尼日利亚人切实可享的益处。他还要求该组织监督立法机关履行承诺，特别是落实拟议的女性专属议席，以及为儿童保护、妇女医疗保健和性别赋权项目提供充足资金。他说：“一个将超过一半人口系统性排除在决定其未来的决策机制之外的民主制度，充其量是一个有缺陷的民主制度，最坏的情况下，则是披着外衣的寡头政治。‘法律的好坏取决于执行。请监督我们。要求《专属议席法案》成为法律。要求儿童保护和妇女健康方面的拨款不仅获得批准，而且得到拨付和使用。’”阿多埃基蒂Afe Babalola大学校长斯马兰达·奥拉林德教授发表主旨演讲时，呼吁加强法律和制度框架，保护妇女和儿童免受新型虐待，尤其是借助技术以及经济脆弱性而滋生的虐待。奥拉林德说，人工智能和数字平台的日益使用带来了新的威胁，包括网络跟踪、网络骚扰、深度伪造图像、冒名身份以及对儿童的剥削。她呼吁政府、司法机关、执法机构、高校、宗教和传统领袖、媒体及公民社会组织加强合作，共同打击基于性别的暴力和儿童虐待。校长还敦促FIDA超越倡导工作，着眼可衡量的成果，并提议建立协作性质的“妇女与儿童司法获取行动框架”，以改善法律保护、数字安全和幸存者支持。埃基蒂州首席法官奥贡莫耶法官在发言中赞扬FIDA选择巴米德莱发表讲座，称他非常适合探讨需要通过立法和政策改革加以应对的新兴问题，以保护妇女和儿童。FIDA埃基蒂州分会主席阿约巴米·奥洛约-理查兹早些时候表示，该组织将继续致力于促进、保护和保障妇女及儿童的权利。她说，不断变化的现实持续给他们的安全、尊严和基本权利带来新挑战，需要更完善的法律、制度和集体应对措施，以确保每个人都能获得司法救济。本文所表达的意见不代表Vanguard报及其任何员工的观点

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/nass.body_zh: 阿布贾——参议院领袖奥佩耶米·巴米德莱表示，审查1999年宪法的国民议会委员会提议在参议院和众议院为女性增设74个议席。该提案还规定，每个州议会为女性保留3个额外议席，且不占用任何现有议席。代表埃基蒂中央选区的巴米德莱于星期一在国际女律师联合会埃基蒂州分会组织的2026年法律周活动上披露了上述信息。他说，这些提案旨在深化女性对尼日利亚政治和治理进程的参与和代表权。巴米德莱也是参议院1999年宪法审查委员会副主席，他在媒体指导部门发表的声明中表示，拟议的专门议席是正在进行的宪法修订程序的一部分。巴米德莱解释说，该提案将在参议院增设37个议席，并在众议院增设37个议席。他表示，如果获得批准，联邦的每个州和联邦首都特区将在国民议会两院中各增设1个议席。他说，委员会还提议每个州议会为女性增设3个议席。巴米德莱表示，这一安排拟实施16年，涵盖4个选举周期，之后将接受全面审查。他称，拟定期限属于日落条款，旨在促进形成更具包容性的政治文化。他说，委员会正在与各州议会沟通；根据宪法，修正案生效必须获得这些议会的同意。巴米德莱表示，此项倡议不具有党派倾向，而是旨在解决女性在决策过程中代表不足的问题。他补充称，在第一夫人奥卢雷米·蒂努布等重要政府人士的倡议和推动下，第10届国民议会对该提案的支持得到加强。在保护妇女和儿童这一更广泛的议题上，巴米德莱表示，法律必须回应新出现的威胁，确保遭受虐待的受害者能够获得保护和司法救济。他说，司法救济应当易于获得、价格可负担、及时且有效，并补充指出，遭受家庭暴力的妇女和遭受虐待的儿童必须得到保护，免受恐吓和进一步伤害。他还呼吁为受害者提供法律援助、医疗照护和社会心理支持，同时应按照正当程序和法治原则追究施害者的责任。出席活动的还有众议院信息与国家_orientation委员会主席史蒂夫·法托巴阁下，以及埃基蒂州议会议长阿德奥耶·阿里巴索耶阁下等。此处发表的意见不代表《Vanguard》报及其任何员工的观点

Unlock these with Subscription Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri will pay a two-day visit to Kathmandu on November 4 and 5, the Ministry of External Affairs announced on Monday (November 2, 2026). This will be the first visit by Mr. Misri to Nepal since Prime Minister Balendra Shah took charge in March this year following the election that was conducted under an interim government. A visit to India by Mr. Shah is understandably part of the agenda that will be discussed when Mr. Misri meets officials in Kathmandu. “Foreign Secretary’s upcoming visit continues the tradition of regular high-level exchanges between the two countries and will help further enhance the comprehensive bilateral partnership,” said the Ministry in an announcement. The visit by Mr. Misri to Kathmandu will be keenly watched as it comes amid a slew of reforms that Nepal’s post-Gen-Z uprising government is in the process of rolling out. Apart from Mr. Shah’s visit to India, Mr. Misri’s conversations in Kathmandu are likely to feature the appointment of a new Ambassador of Nepal to New Delhi. Nepali Embassy has been without an Ambassador for several months since the previous Ambassador, Shankar Prasad Sharma, returned home. Nepali diplomatic sources told The Hindu earlier that Kathmandu was waiting for the agrément (diplomatic approval) for new envoy Nischal Nath Pandey to take charge in the embassy here. India’s continued assistance to the disaster in Bhote Koshi river is also expected to be on the agenda. Even as Mr. Misri's visit was being announced by the Ministry, a welfare association of former Indian Army soldiers took out a protest in Kathmandu on Monday (November 2) demanding that Gurkha recruitment into the Indian Army be resumed. Recruitment of Gurkha soldiers remains suspended since the Agnipath scheme was introduced by the Government of India. The Hindu had earlier reported that Mr. Misri was expected to visit Nepal in May, but the visit was postponed ostensibly because Mr. Shah had prioritised domestic challenges. The India visit by Mr. Shah, if it materialises, will be the first bilateral visit abroad by the leader who came into prominence during the September 2025 Gen-Z uprising that overthrew the government of Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli. Mr. Misri had visited Kathmandu previously for two days in August 2025 and had met Mr. Oli. In the past few months, India has hosted Nepal’s Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal, Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, and Home Minister Sudan Gurung, who visited Delhi to participate in the first BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) meet held on October 13, 2026. India has also hosted the head of the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) Rabi Lamichhane in the first week of June when he met Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Lamichhane paid a personal visit to India last week to pray at the pilgrimage centres in Kainchi Dham in Uttarakhand and the Kamakhya temple in Guwahati. Mr. Lamichhane had described this visit as “personal and not political”. “There are no political meetings planned. 印度外交部长兼常秘vikram Misri将于11月4日至5日对加德满都进行为期两天的访问。印度外交部于11月2日（星期一）宣布了这一消息。这将是Misri先生自总理Balendra Shah今年3月在临时政府主持的选举后就任以来首次访问尼泊尔。

可以理解，Misri先生在加德满都会见官员时，Shah先生访印将是讨论议程的一部分。印度外交部在公告中表示：“外交部长即将进行的访问延续了两国定期开展高层互动的传统，将有助于进一步提升两国全面双边伙伴关系。”

Misri先生此次访问加德满都将受到密切关注，因为尼泊尔“Gen-Z”起义后的政府正在推行一系列改革。除了Shah先生访印外，Misri先生在加德满都的会谈预计将涉及任命尼泊尔新任驻新德里大使。自上一任大使Shankar Prasad Sharma回国后，尼泊尔大使馆已数月没有大使。尼泊尔外交消息人士此前告诉《The Hindu》，加德满都正在等待新任特使Nischal Nath Pandey获准（外交批准）赴任这里。印度继续援助Bhote Koshi河流灾后重建，预计也将列入议程。

在印度外交部宣布Misri先生访尼行程之际，一名前印度陆军士兵福利协会于11月2日（星期一）在加德满都举行抗议，要求恢复为印度陆军招募廓尔喀士兵。自印度政府推出Agnipath计划以来，廓尔喀士兵招募一直处于暂停状态。

《The Hindu》此前报道称，Misri先生原定于5月访问尼泊尔，但此次访问表面上是因Shah先生优先处理国内挑战而推迟。

如果Shah先生访印成行，这将是这位领导人在2025年9月推翻总理K.P. Sharma Oli政府的“Gen-Z”起义中崭露头角后首次出访外国进行双边访问。Misri先生此前曾于2025年8月访问加德满都两天，并会见了Oli先生。

过去几个月，印度接待了尼泊尔外长Sisir Khanal、财政部长Swarnim Wagle和内政部长Sudan Gurung，他们赴德里参加了10月13日举行的首届BIMSTEC（孟加拉湾多部门技术经济合作倡议）会议。

印度还在6月第一周接待了执政的Rastriya Swatantra Party（RSP）领导人Rabi Lamichhane，期间他会见了总理Narendra Modi。Lamichhane先生上周还对印度进行私人访问，前往北阿坎德邦Kainchi Dham的朝圣中心和古瓦哈提的Kamakhya寺祈祷。Lamichhane先生将此次访问描述为“私人访问，并非政治访问”。

Lamichhane先生在出发前表示：“目前没有安排任何政治会谈。由于这是一次私人访问，我呼吁人们不要对此作政治解读。”

https://www.myjoyonline.com/goldbod-amon.body: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has increased the number of companies admitted into its virtual asset regulatory sandbox from 11 to 20 as it gathers information to guide the regulation of digital asset services in Ghana. The expansion is intended to give the regulator a broader understanding of the services being offered under the Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2025 (Act 1154), and help shape the licensing framework for the sector. Speaking at the Africa Virtual Assets Summit 2026, the Acting Director-General of the SEC, Dr James Klutse Avedzi, said the additional companies would provide the regulator with more data on the different activities taking place in the virtual asset industry. He identified tokenisation as one of the services covered by the regulatory framework, describing it as an established licensing category. “Tokenisation is an explicit licensing category, not an afterthought,” he said. Tokenisation involves converting ownership rights or interests in physical or financial assets into digital tokens that can be recorded and transferred using blockchain technology. Dr Avedzi disclosed that live tokenisation pilot projects were already underway, with Ghana exploring how blockchain technology could help formalise its largely informal gold supply chain. “Ghana is deliberately testing whether blockchain can formalise its large, partly informal gold supply chain,” he said. Some of the companies admitted into the expanded sandbox include Africoin Ghana, the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), The Blue Penguin Company, HSB Global Fintech and BSystems. Dr Avedzi said companies that satisfy the required compliance standards could apply for full licences after completing their participation in the sandbox. He explained that information gathered during the testing period would help the SEC develop licensing requirements and regulatory rules for the different virtual asset services. Despite the expansion of the sandbox, Dr Avedzi said several regulatory requirements for tokenised securities were still being developed. These include capital requirements, custody standards, disclosure obligations and investor protection measures. He also identified outstanding legal questions concerning property and title rights, the enforceability of claims represented by digital tokens, and the regulation of secondary markets for tokenised real-world assets. On the legislative front, he said the Securities Industry Act, 2016 (Act 929), was being amended to address potential classification challenges involving tokenised instruments. Dr Avedzi said Ghana was still completing its regulatory strategy and legislative framework, even as supervised testing of virtual asset services continued. A fully operational licensing regime is yet to be established. He projected that the first group of companies could graduate from the sandbox and obtain full licences between late 2026 and early 2027
https://www.myjoyonline.com/goldbod-amon.title_zh: 加纳黄金局成为SEC扩大后的虚拟资产监管沙盒中的20家公司之一
https://www.myjoyonline.com/goldbod-amon.body_zh: 证券交易委员会（SEC）已将获准进入其虚拟资产监管沙盒的公司数量从11家增至20家，以收集信息并指导加纳数字资产服务的监管工作。此次扩容旨在让监管机构更全面地了解《2025年虚拟资产服务提供商法》（第1154号法案）下提供的各项服务，并帮助制定该行业的许可框架。在2026年非洲虚拟资产峰会上，SEC代理总干事詹姆斯·克卢策·阿韦齐博士表示，新增公司将为监管机构提供更多数据，以了解虚拟资产行业中开展的不同业务。他指出，资产代币化是监管框架涵盖的服务之一，并将其描述为一个已经确立的许可类别。他说：“资产代币化是一个明确的许可类别，而非事后附加的事项。”资产代币化是指将实物资产或金融资产的所有权权利或权益转换为数字代币，并利用区块链技术进行记录和转让。阿韦齐博士透露，资产代币化试点项目已经在进行，加纳正在探索区块链技术如何帮助其规模庞大且部分非正式化的黄金供应链实现正规化。他说：“加纳正在有意识地测试区块链能否使规模庞大、部分非正式的黄金供应链正规化。”获准进入扩容后沙盒的公司包括Africoin Ghana、加纳黄金局（GoldBod）、The Blue Penguin Company、HSB Global Fintech和BSystems。阿韦齐博士表示，满足所需合规标准的公司完成沙盒参与计划后，可以申请完整许可证。他 explained? 在测试期间收集的信息将帮助SEC制定不同虚拟资产服务的许可要求和监管规则。尽管沙盒已经扩容，阿韦齐博士表示，代币化证券的若干监管要求仍在制定之中，包括资本要求、托管标准、披露义务和投资者保护措施。他还指出了一些尚待解决的法律问题，涉及财产权和所有权、数字代币所代表权利主张的可执行性，以及代币化现实世界资产二级市场的监管。在立法方面，他表示，《2016年证券行业法》（第929号法案）正在修订，以解决代币化工具可能面临的分类难题。阿韦齐博士表示，尽管虚拟资产服务的受监管测试仍在继续，加纳仍在完善其监管战略和立法框架。全面运行的许可制度尚未建立。他预计，首批公司将在2026年末至2027年初期间完成沙盒计划并取得完整许可证

https://www.myjoyonline.com/parliaments-.summary: The Parliamentary Committee on Human Rights has called on the Ministry of Education, the Ghana Education Service (GES) and the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE) to reintroduce and strengthen safe disciplinary standards in second-cycle institutions across the country. It stressed the urgent need to reintroduce safe disciplinary standards to address the situation, warning that failure to do so could undermine Ghana’s efforts to achieve Sustainable Development Goal 4, which focuses on quality education.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/parliaments-.summary_zh: 人权议会委员会已呼吁教育部、加纳教育局（GES）和国家公民教育委员会（NCCE），在全国中等教育机构中重新推行并强化安全的纪律标准。委员会强调，为应对当前局势，迫切需要重新推行安全的纪律标准，并警告称，若不这样做，可能削弱加纳实现可持续发展目标4的努力，而该目标侧重于优质教育。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/parliaments-.body: The Parliamentary Committee on Human Rights has called on the Ministry of Education, the Ghana Education Service (GES) and the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE) to reintroduce and strengthen safe disciplinary standards in second-cycle institutions across the country. The call follows a viral video allegedly showing some teachers of Techiman Senior High School assaulting a student, an incident the Committee has described as disturbing. In a press release issued on Monday, November 2, and signed by its Chairman, Ernest Yaw Anim, the Committee expressed concern over what it described as the increasing trend of indiscipline in second-cycle institutions, involving headteachers, housemasters, teachers and students. “The Committee takes a strong view of such action, as well as the increasing rate and trend of indiscipline stemming from second-cycle institutions in Ghana,” the statement said. It stressed the urgent need to reintroduce safe disciplinary standards to address the situation, warning that failure to do so could undermine Ghana’s efforts to achieve Sustainable Development Goal 4, which focuses on quality education. “The Committee believes there is an urgent need for the reintroduction of safe disciplinary standard measures to curb the rising culture of indiscipline,” it stated. The Committee further noted that the situation had implications for the protection of children’s rights under domestic and international laws, including Article 25(1) of the 1992 Constitution, Section 8 of the Children’s Act, 1998 (Act 560), and Article 28(2) of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. Reaffirming its commitment to protecting the right to education, the Committee said it remained “deeply committed to preserving the sanctity of Education in Ghana” and ensuring that quality education was guaranteed as a fundamental human right for all
https://www.myjoyonline.com/parliaments-.title_zh: 议会人权委员会呼吁在中学重新推行安全的惩戒措施
https://www.myjoyonline.com/parliaments-.body_zh: 国会人权委员会已呼吁教育部、加纳教育署（GES）和国家公民教育委员会（NCCE），在全国中等教育机构中重新推行并加强安全的纪律标准。此前，一段据称显示特奇曼高级中学部分教师殴打学生的视频在网上广泛传播，委员会称这一事件令人不安。委员会在11月2日星期一发布的新闻公报中宣布了这一呼吁，公报由委员会主席欧内斯特·亚奥·阿宁签署。委员会对所谓的全国中等教育机构中纪律松弛现象日益加剧表示担忧，这种情况涉及校长、宿舍管理员、教师和学生。公报称：“委员会严厉谴责此类行为，也谴责加纳中等教育机构中源自纪律松弛且不断上升的比例和趋势。”委员会强调，必须 urgently 重新推行安全的纪律标准以应对这一问题，并警告称，如不采取措施，可能削弱加纳实现可持续发展目标4的努力，该目标侧重于优质教育。委员会表示：“委员会认为，迫切需要重新推行安全纪律标准措施，以遏制日益上升的纪律松弛文化。”委员会还指出，这一情况影响到依据国内法和国际法保护儿童权利，包括1992年《宪法》第25(1)条、1998年《儿童法》（第560号法案）第8条以及《联合国儿童权利公约》第28(2)条。委员会重申其保护受教育权的承诺，表示仍“深切致力于维护加纳教育的庄严性”，并确保所有人作为基本人权都能获得优质教育
